items.title: CAN 2027 : trois pays, un projet de visa commun
items.description: Le Kenya, la Tanzanie et l’Ouganda planchent sur la mise en place d’un dispositif de visa commun destiné à faciliter les déplacements des supporters entre les trois pays à l’occasion de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2027, a annoncé mardi la présidente du Conseil des ministres de la Communauté d’Afrique de l’Est (CAE), Rebecca Alitwala Kadaga. Cette annonce intervient à l’occasion d’une visite d’inspection du stade Arusha Pamoja par des membres de l’Assemblée législative de l’Afrique de l’Est (EALA), en présence de Mme Kadaga, également première vice-Première ministre ougandaise et ministre chargée des Affaires de la CAE. À cette occasion, Mme Kadaga a indiqué que les trois pays hôtes œuvrent à l’élaboration d’un régime de visa spécial visant à faciliter la circulation des supporters durant la compétition, notant que ce dispositif leur permettrait d’assister à des rencontres dans différents pays tout en découvrant les sites touristiques de la région. Cette initiative pourrait également générer des retombées économiques au profit des établissements hôteliers, des voyagistes, des transporteurs et des autres prestataires de services liés au tourisme. Toutefois, l’efficacité de ce mécanisme dépendra des modalités définitives du visa et de leur mise en œuvre effective aux postes-frontières, a souligné Abdullah Makame, membre de l’EALA. Par ailleurs, la délégation a été informée que les travaux de construction du stade Arusha Pamoja, dont la capacité prévisionnelle est d’environ 32.500 places, avaient atteint un taux d’avancement de 95 %. La 36e édition de la CAN se tiendra du 19 juin au 17 juillet 2027 au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda. Il s’agira de la première édition de cette compétition continentale organisée conjointement par trois pays. items.title: Tebboune annonce la fabrication d’une voiture algérienne en 2028
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune , a rencontré les chefs d’entreprises ce mercredi 14 octobre au CIC d’Alger. Durant cette rencontre, la troisième du genre en trois ans, le chef de l’État a évoqué la fabrication d’une voiture algérienne à l’horizon 2028. « Si les choses se déroulent comme nous les avons planifiées avec les Allemands et les Italiens, nous aurons une voiture algérienne d’ici la fin 2028, avec une boîte de vitesses algérienne et des pneumatiques algériens, et pas seulement du gonflage de pneus. C’est un pari que nous tiendrons », a affirmé le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Tebboune sur la voiture algérienne : « C’est un pari que nous tiendrons » L’Algérie a lancé un vaste chantier pour se doter d’une véritable industrie automobile capable de fabriquer des véhicules avec un taux d’intégration de 30 %. Ce chantier a été lancé en 2023 avec l’installation de la marque Fiat du groupe Stellantis, qui a ouvert une usine à Oran, où elle fabrique le modèle Doblo tôlé et panoramique. Depuis septembre 2025, Fiat Algérie a lancé la fabrication de la Grande Panda en mode CKD, une première pour l’industrie automobile algérienne. Cette voiture, qui n’est pas encore sortie des chaînes, devrait atteindre un taux d’intégration de 30 %. D’autres constructeurs automobiles de taille mondiale comme Hyundai et Chery ont annoncé des projets de fabrication de voitures en Algérie. Opel, une autre marque du groupe Stellantis, a fait part, il y a quelques mois, d’un projet de fabrication de voitures et de moteurs en Algérie. Entre-temps, l’Algérie a lancé des usines de fabrication de composants plastiques, de plaquettes de frein et de carrosseries pour véhicules. L’article Tebboune annonce la fabrication d’une voiture algérienne en 2028 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: GTEC’s letter directing public universities to reopen by October 16 is unprofessional – GAUA
items.description: The Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has criticised the tone of a directive by the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) ordering public universities to reopen by Friday and resume academic work by Monday at the latest. Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Newsnight, GAUA President Reverend Amoah Karikari described the language of the letter as “unprofessional” and said the commission should respect the governance structures of public universities. He said GAUA had no objection to GTEC directing universities under its regulatory authority to resume operations but insisted that the directive would not automatically end the association’s strike. “We don’t have a problem. But I must be quick to say that the tone of the letter is not professional,” he said. “GTEC cannot and should not behave as if it is a headmaster remote controlling vice chancellors and university council,” he added. He clarified that the association did not necessarily feel insulted by the letter but considered its language excessive. The GAUA president also maintained that the association would call off its strike only after receiving a letter from the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) addressing its market premium demand. He explained that this was a condition agreed upon at the association’s last meeting with the Minister of Education. His comments follow a directive from the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) ordering all public universities to reopen by Friday and resume academic work by Monday at the latest.

items.title: Suspect in viral video assaulting wife jailed for 3 months
items.description: A 30-year-old farmer, Emmanuel Kwofie, has been sentenced to three months’ imprisonment with hard labour for assaulting his wife in an incident that went viral on social media. This was contained in a statement issued by the Western Regional Police Command of the Ghana Police Service. It said the Agona Nkwanta District Police Command secured his conviction on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, after he pleaded guilty to the assault charge before the Agona Nkwanta District Court. Police investigations established that Kwofie, who is married to Diana Mensah, a second-hand clothing trader, accused her of having an extramarital affair before subjecting her to a severe beating on October 8, 2026. The couple lives together at Domeabra in the Agona Nkwanta Municipality. Kwofie was arrested on October 12, 2026, and subsequently arraigned before the court on October 14. The case was presided over by Kuma Selorm Dzata, who convicted the accused on his own plea and sentenced him to three months’ imprisonment with hard labour.

items.title: GAUA insists strike will end only after Fair Wages addresses market premium issue
items.description: President of the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA), Reverend Amoah Karikari, says it will call off its strike only after receiving a formal letter from the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) on its market premium demand. He said the association agreed to suspend the industrial action on the condition that the commission provides the required communication on the outstanding issue. His comments follow a directive from the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) ordering all public universities to reopen by Friday and resume academic work by Monday at the latest. Speaking on Joy fm’s Newsnight, Reverend Karikari said GAUA had no objection to GTEC directing universities under its regulatory authority to resume operations but maintained that the directive would not automatically end the strike. “GTEC is our regulator and they can go ahead to direct universities that they regulate to resume work. But we are on strike. So if the Deputy Director-General of GTEC, who issued the reopening directive under the instruction of the Education Minister, who was present at the meetig was listening well and was attentive at the meeting, we agreed that we call off the strike based on a condition precedent: that we receive a letter from Fair Wages on our market premium issue,” he said. Reverend Karikari also criticised the tone of GTEC’s letter, describing its language as unprofessional and excessive in its approach to university management. He argued that public universities are governed by their respective councils and that GTEC should not act as though it has direct control over vice-chancellors and university councils. “GTEC cannot and should not behave as if it is a headmaster remote controlling vice chancellors and university council,” he said. The GAUA president, however, clarified that the association did not necessarily feel insulted by the letter but objected to what he considered overreaching language. GAUA began its nationwide strike in August over salary disparities and conditions of service. One major concern is the market premium, which the association says has fallen behind that of teaching staff. The strike has disrupted administrative operations in public universities, with GAUA maintaining that progress on its market premium demand is necessary before it can suspend the industrial action.

items.title: Kpemka seeks compensation as he sues BOST over alleged unlawful termination
items.description: Former Deputy Managing Director of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited (BOST), Joseph Dindiok Kpemka, has sued the company over what he describes as the unlawful termination of his appointment. His lawyer, Patrick Fafali Azameti, says BOST failed to formally terminate his client’s appointment after the change of government in 2025, despite repeated attempts to clarify his employment status and obtain his outstanding entitlements. The lawyer told told Accra-based Citi FM on Wednesday that some individuals entered Mr Kpemka’s office after the change of government and asked him to leave and hand over to company officers. He said his client subsequently made several attempts to secure his outstanding benefits but was unsuccessful, leaving him with no option but to seek redress in court. “After several demands on BOST to pay him his entitled benefits failed, he was left with no option but to take the matter to court for the appropriate remedy,” he said. Mr Azameti stressed that his client had not received any official communication confirming the termination of his appointment. “The interesting part of it is that there was no official or formal communication of termination,” he said. According to the lawyer, Mr Kpemka’s employment agreement specified the terms and conditions of his service, including the procedure BOST was required to follow to terminate his appointment. He said the agreement also provided for certain benefits and remuneration due to his client. Mr Kpemka is seeking compensation through the legal action against the company.

items.title: 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu
items.description: Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe. Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday. He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls. Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance. In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern. In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership. Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.” He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies. The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance. “From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.” Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear. “The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued. According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular. “He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.” Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.” He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term. The post 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists
items.description: By Dickson Omobola National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Felix Muoka, has insisted that Nigeria and Nigerians are better off than ever before, saying the party will win the 2027 presidential election based on its positive records. Muoka said the APC was working hard to secure voters’ support, adding that the party would not take Nigerians’ votes for granted. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Thursday, he said the party’s preparations and campaign efforts were aimed at securing as many votes as possible in the next general elections. He said: “Qualitatively speaking, our country is better. Nigerians are better today than they have ever been. Is there a country that has transited from this depressed economy, like we have had for decades, to that level of prosperity that didn’t go through these stages? “Nigerians also understand that. So what the president has done is to give this country a fighting chance, not just at recovery, but at building the prospects for sustainable prosperity.” On the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, he said: “What you saw today and what we’ve been up to is really taking ourselves seriously. If we thought this was all said and done, we wouldn’t put in this level of energy and work in an effort to really get to the last vote within the electorate. We are not taking this for granted. We’re taking it very seriously. I’m sure that if our party was docile and we were doing nothing to campaign or put out our information, you would also bring me here to say that we had been very docile. We’re a political party. “We are a party for a reason. We are in this to compete with other political parties and to win the support of Nigerians. Since 2023, there’s a reason that our party has been very successful. Since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically all elections in which we have contested. There’s a reason for that. It’s because we prepare. We do our homework. “Nigerians bought in and voted for our party massively in 2023. We won that election, even though there are elements who want to claim that they won without evidence. But we won that election without question. As I said a few minutes ago, in every other election that has been called since then, Nigerians voted, not Indians. Nigerians voted in all the other elections since 2023. We won by upwards of 90 per cent. “Let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. Already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election in which the APC is governing, not just at the centre, but in so many states in our country.” On the APC’s chances in 2027, he said: “We will win the election. We are working hard to win the election. I think that Nigerians are going to stand tall, shoulder to shoulder with the APC to win the next election.” Vanguard News The post Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kobe Boujee joins Olympics.com team for Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games
items.description: Ghanaian content creator Kobe Boujee has been selected as a Content Contributor and Producer, joining the Olympics.com team ahead of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, set to take place from October 31 to November 13. In his role, Kobe Boujee will work alongside the Olympics.com team to produce original digital content capturing the spirit, culture and competition of the first Youth Olympic Games to be held on African soil. His contributions will span the lead-up to the Games and continue through live coverage in Dakar, offering audiences an authentic, creator-led lens on the event. Known for his engaging storytelling style and strong connection with young audiences across Africa, Kobe Boujee brings a distinct voice to the Olympics.com team — one built on relatability, African stories and genuine cultural insights. “Being part of the Olympics.com team for Dakar 2026 is an incredible honour,” said Kobe Boujee. “This is bigger than content for me. it’s about showing young people across Africa that this stage belongs to us too. I’m ready to bring people along on this journey, every step of the way.” As part of his role, Kobe Boujee will produce a mix of video content, behind-the-scenes features and athlete-focused storytelling for Olympics.com’s digital platforms, with select content also shared across his own channels. “Growing up, the Olympics always felt like something happening far away. Now it’s happening on our continent, and I get to help tell that story. My focus is on the athletes, the young people out there competing, and making sure their stories are seen and felt, not just their results.” Audiences are encouraged to follow Kobe Boujee’s coverage throughout the Games on the Olympics.com website and app, where his content will be featured as part of the official Dakar 2026 digital experience. Kobe Boujee is expected to join the team in Dakar some days before the start of the Games.

items.title: Slaty egret’s shifting nesting sites offer clues to changing ecosystems
items.description: Scientists studying a rare African waterbird in Botswana’s Okavango Delta have found that previously established nesting sites are no longer being used, while new breeding locations have been identified, offering clues to how environmental changes may be affecting one of Africa’s most important wetland ecosystems. The findings from surveys conducted in 2025 and 2026 show a changing pattern in the breeding distribution of the vulnerable slaty egret ( Egretta vinaceigula ), a small, shy wading bird found mainly in southern Africa. Only about 3,000 slaty egrets are estimated to remain in the Okavango Delta, their principal stronghold. Researchers found no nesting birds at a major breeding site in the western part of the Delta that had been examined in 2025. In the Jao Conservancy, two of four previously identified nesting sites had also disappeared. One site had been affected by fire, while another was damaged after elephants used the area to cool themselves following a summer heatwave. But the surveys also revealed new nesting locations elsewhere in the Delta, including an island concealed by vegetation where researchers found three bluish eggs. The contrasting findings suggest that the birds may be changing where they breed as conditions in the wetland shift. Researchers say, however, that further observations are needed to determine whether the changes reflect a longer-term pattern and what they mean for the species’ population. A sensitive indicator of environmental change A senior wildlife biologist with Botswana’s Department of Wildlife and National Parks, Monei Onalethatai, said the slaty egret was particularly sensitive to disturbances and changes in its surroundings. “The slaty egret is so sensitive to environmental disturbances and to ecosystem changes. “Whatever happens in the ecosystem will necessarily reflect in the distribution and the presence of the bird,” she said. The bird’s restricted range makes these observations particularly important to conservationists seeking to understand changes in the Okavango Delta. Executive Officer of the Agreement on the Conservation of African-Eurasian Migratory Waterbirds (AEWA), Sergey Dereliev, said the species was endemic to southern Africa, with its distribution concentrated in the Okavango Delta and neighbouring floodplains. He said the bird could be found in the Delta and adjacent floodplains in the Okavango and Zambezi river basins. “ The slaty egret is a long-legged wading bird which is endemic to southern Africa, and its uniqueness lies in the fact that it’s only possible to see this bird in the Okavango Delta and some adjacent floodplains in the Okavango and Zambezi river basins.” Researchers are monitoring its population and breeding success to improve understanding of the pressures affecting the species and its habitat. How water shapes breeding conditions The Okavango is an inland delta whose waters never reach the ocean. Floodwaters originating from rainfall in Angola’s highlands flow south into Botswana, spreading across a network of channels, floodplains, lagoons and islands before eventually evaporating or disappearing into the Kalahari. The annual flood, which typically flows through the Delta between June and August, helps determine the availability of water and habitat for wildlife. According to the United Nations, the seasonal flood pulse supports more than 400 bird species, including migratory birds arriving from Europe and northern Asia. Some use the Delta as a stopover during longer journeys, while others remain through the northern winter. Zebras, buffalo, elephants, wildebeest and numerous fish species also depend on the wider ecosystem. For the slaty egret, the extent of flooding can influence breeding conditions. The birds tend to nest on islands or in areas surrounded by water, which help protect them from disturbances. Changes in water levels can affect the availability of suitable nesting locations, while vegetation, food supplies and disturbance can determine whether a particular site remains suitable for breeding. In 2026, the Okavango experienced an unusually large flood. Researchers had expected the additional water might allow slaty egrets to expand their breeding grounds into new areas. The findings, however, presented a more complicated picture. Some established nesting sites were empty or had disappeared, while new sites were found elsewhere. The observations suggest that the relationship between flooding and breeding habitat may change conditions across the Delta without making every location suitable for nesting. Why repeated surveys matter Researchers have used satellite imagery and field observations to identify breeding locations and examine how vegetation, water availability and habitat conditions relate to the birds’ distribution. The latest surveys have highlighted the need to revisit known nesting sites while searching for previously unrecorded ones. Scientists are still collecting evidence and say the available observations are insufficient to establish a population trend or identify a single cause for the changes in breeding distribution. Repeated monitoring will be needed to determine whether the birds are making temporary adjustments to changing conditions or whether their movement away from established nesting sites represents a more persistent pattern. The findings also underline the importance of looking beyond individual breeding colonies. A site that was suitable in one year may no longer support nesting in another, while a previously overlooked location may become important under different conditions. The slaty egret’s distribution could therefore provide useful evidence of environmental changes across the Delta, although researchers need further data to establish how closely particular changes in the bird’s breeding patterns correspond with changes in the wider ecosystem. Protecting the species also requires cooperation between countries that share the river systems on which its habitat depends. Climate change and water management across national borders can affect the availability and distribution of water, making regional collaboration important for wetland conservation. For researchers, the disappearance of a nesting colony deserves attention even when birds are found elsewhere. Likewise, the discovery of a new colony is important without necessarily indicating that the species is thriving. Understanding why these locations become suitable or unsuitable over time could help scientists assess the pressures facing the slaty egret and guide efforts to protect the Okavango Delta’s wildlife and habitats.

items.title: First phase of arrears for promoted teachers to be paid on Friday – Haruna Iddrisu announces
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has announced that the government would honour its promise to pay promoted teachers their due salaries by the end of October 2026. He indicated that the first phase of payment would be made by Friday the 16th, based on the new grades of the promoted teachers. He was speaking at the 64th Annual National Conference of the Conference of Heads of Assisted Secondary Schools (CHASS) in Ho, in the Volta Region. “But let me start with an assurance GNAT, and all of the people seated here, and NAGRAT, that on Friday, the 16th of October, I want to walk with my chest and neck high government will honor the first phase of the payment of the outstanding arrears in respect of promotion for the first category of 52,000 all promoted teachers.” “The Controller and Accountant General will honour it on Friday. Then the rest will be pushed in October. So, at the end of October, all of you will receive your salaries on the new grade of promoted teachers.”, he said. These among other issues were the teacher unions used a strike action as a bargaining chip to resolve, pushing for better conditions of service. Ghana Association of University Administrators Mr Haruna said that the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) is liaising with the Finance Ministry to resolve the issue of market premium and the one-time research allowance, which led to a strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators. He expressed optimism that the strike action would be called off by Friday, allowing the universities to reopen after the government reaches a consensus with the Association’s leadership. “Let me assure you that government will do everything possible for the strike to be called off by close of work on Friday. Will do everything possible, but we are also urging God that they should act in good faith in dealing with the government as an employer. “The number of the issues they placed before us: one was to rectify the issue of market premium and parity with some other members, even including Rutak. The Fair Wages and Salaries Commission will respond to them by close of work on Friday, and it will be adequate enough.” “On the outstanding issues of their one-off cook and research allowance, I have seen the warrant signed by the Honorable Minister for Finance for 12 million Ghana cedis to honour that particular pledge. The other I shared a letter with their leadership Sunday and Karikare was about 40% allowance.” “The other matters are matters that they can be negotiated. So be assured, it is a decision of government that the investors should all be open this weekend. All investors. in Ghana must be open for business in order that we don’t lose the academic calendar”, he assured.

items.title: FG fixes August 2027 deadline for WAEC, NECO results
items.description: By Joseph Erunke The Federal Government has proposed a new examination timetable that will see candidates sitting the 2027 West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO) and other major external examinations receive their results by August, ahead of the September admission process into tertiary institutions. Under the proposed schedule, the government is seeking to end delays in the release of examination results that could disrupt candidates’ transition from secondary schools to universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. A statement on Wednesday night by the Director, Press and Public Relations of the Federal Ministry of Education, Boriowo Folasade, said the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, disclosed the plan during a meeting with heads and representatives of examination bodies at the Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja. “The meeting focused on harmonising examination schedules, preventing clashes among major examinations and ensuring that results are processed and released within agreed timelines, “the statement said. According to the proposed timetable, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) will conduct the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) from March 15 to 25, with results expected in the same month. NECO’s Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) is scheduled to hold from April 1 to May 14, while WAEC’s West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) will run from May 11 to June 18. Both NECO and WAEC are expected to release their results in August 2027. The National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examination is proposed for June 1 to July 5, while the National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS) examination will hold from June 10 to July 9. Results from both examinations are also expected in August. The proposed schedule places the examination bodies under pressure to complete their respective processes in time to meet the government’s August results-release target. The Federal Ministry of Education said the initiative was part of the education reform agenda of the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, under the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), which seeks to improve efficiency, coordination and educational outcomes. It added that engagement with examination bodies would continue to ensure compliance with the proposed timelines, strengthen accountability and align the release of results with tertiary admission schedules. The government, under President Bola Tinubu, said it remained committed to reforms that would improve the efficiency of the education system and expand timely access to tertiary education. However, the timetable remains proposed, with the success of the plan depending on effective coordination among the examination bodies and their ability to meet the agreed deadlines. If implemented as planned, the initiative could give candidates and their parents greater certainty over the transition from secondary school examinations to tertiary admissions, while reducing disruptions caused by late results. items.title: Achakzai sees governor's rule next being imposed in Sindh, over water and mines
items.description: Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai warned on Wednesday that governor’s rule would be imposed next in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”, urging the Centre to give provinces their rights and resources. He was speaking in the National Assembly, where a resolution endorsing the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday was passed . The federal government cited the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism as the reason for imposing governor’s rule in KP. In days preceding the development, political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, mainly the PTI, had remained high after the party announced a long march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. However, the march, initially planned for Islamabad, remained confined to KP until it fizzled out with the imposition of governor’s rule in the province. In his address, Achakzai said KP’s “mistake is that it saved itself with the help of its people”. He also drew a comparison between the current situation with regards to KP and the one witnessed at the time of the creation of Bangladesh. He also assailed the government for depriving the PTI of its election symbol ahead of the 2024 general elections. “And the mistake of his (Imran’s) party’s workers was that they contested the elections on 200 different symbols and turned your own game around on you. You are meting out the punishment for that? You are punishing 240 million people of Pakistan for that?” The opposition leader also pointed out that Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the chief minister after the imposition of governor’s rule and had been leading the PTI’s march, had not resorted to violence or using expletives in his call for the protest. He went on to say, “When you try to snatch our right to self-determination, our right to vote, we all will stand against you. All of us, all provinces.” Noting the participation of the PPP, which is in power in Sindh, Achakzai said it pained him. He then warned that governor’s rule would next be imposed in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”. “And then you will recall your mistake,” he said, noting however that there was still time to rectify mistakes. “Reverse these decisions,” Achakzai said, urging that Parliament be made the centre of power. “And Pakistan will be saved.” He warned that when the “state turns against its own people, they are compelled to look elsewhere”. The opposition also criticised the government over the country’s economic situation. “You are looting this country’s resources […] Have some mercy on this country. […] This country is drowning because of our mistakes. There is only one way to save it: through its Constitution and Parliament and by having a democratic system,” he asserted. Achakzai also lamented the fact the Parliament was not taken into confidence over decisions related to foreign affairs, and that Pakistan had strained ties with most of its neighbours. On Imran, who has not been allowed meetings with his family and associates for a long time, Achakzai said: “Which provision of the Constitution … places a restriction on meetings with the most popular leader of the country?” He assured that if meetings were arranged with Imran, “we will just try to assess his health condition and will try to resolve matter between you. We promise we will meet him and not tell anyone. […] Have some sense. Negotiate.” He concluded his address by declaring that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP was wrong.

items.title: Tebboune face aux patrons : discours apaisé et bilan satisfaisant de l’économie algérienne
items.description: Troisième rencontre en trois ans du président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune , avec les opérateurs économiques, réunis ce mercredi 14 octobre au Centre international des conférences (CIC) d’Alger à l’initiative du Conseil du renouveau économique algérien (CREA). Dans un discours de 45 minutes, au ton apaisé, Abdelmadjid Tebboune a fait un état des lieux de l'économie algérienne , a exprimé son satisfecit de ce qui a été fait et a réitéré sa confiance aux chefs d'entreprise. Les difficultés qui subsistent sont dues au passage « qui n'est pas toujours facile » d’une économie dirigée à une économie de marché. Les pratiques néfastes qui continuent à être déplorées sont le fait de « la minorité des minorités ». Tebboune remonte le moral aux chefs d'entreprise Le président a fait le choix d’un discours apaisé pour booster le moral des patrons qui en ont plus que jamais besoin dans une conjoncture internationale difficile et au moment où la stratégie de relance et de diversification de l'économie est en « passe d'atteindre tous ses objectifs », à l’orée de « l’année pivot » 2027. Ceux qui s'attendaient à entendre la colère du président, à la suite de l'affaire des exagérations dans les demandes d’importation formulées par certains opérateurs, n'ont pas vu juste. L'affaire a été divulguée début septembre par le ministère du Commerce extérieur et avait provoqué une réunion au sommet présidée par le chef de l’État en personne. Des entreprises, employant parfois une ou deux personnes, ont introduit des demandes d’importation d’une valeur cumulée de 130 milliards de dollars. Tebboune appelle à combattre ensemble les « parasites » Dans son discours de ce mercredi, Tebboune a évidemment évoqué ce dépassement, sans toutefois trop s’y attarder et, surtout, sans en faire le reproche à toute la sphère économique. Au contraire, il a appelé les opérateurs à contribuer à débusquer et à lutter contre ces pratiques et leurs auteurs. « Le parasite qui n'a pas compris que l’Algérie a changé, nous devons le combattre ensemble », a-t-il dit. Ce ne sont pas, du reste, ces pratiques isolées qui peuvent ternir l'image des chefs d'entreprise, véritables « partenaires stratégiques de l’État », a reconnu le président qui a dénoncé les « tentatives d’épuiser les réserves de devises du pays ». Les chiffres de la transformation Pour le reste, les chiffres sont là pour plaider la bonne marche de l'économie nationale et de ses acteurs qui sont en passe de doter l’Algérie, « définitivement, d’une économie nouvelle et forte en 2027 ». Les importations ont été réduites « de manière structurelle » de 62 à 40-42 milliards de dollars grâce à l'apport de la production locale ; la production pharmaceutique couvre 84 % des besoins du pays contre à peine 10 % il n’y a pas longtemps ; l'industrie contribue désormais à 10 % du PIB après un long « désert industriel », la perspective d'avoir une « voiture algérienne » en 2028… En tout cas, « il y a une grande différence entre 2020 et aujourd'hui », et l'économie algérienne, qui était « désarticulée », est devenue « la troisième économie d’Afrique », et « pourquoi pas la première » à terme. L'Algérie enregistre aussi des taux de croissance appréciables, 3,8 % en 2025 et des prévisions à 4 % en 2026. Avant le chef de l'État, le ministre des Finances, Mohamed Lamine Lebbou, avait livré les chiffres du PIB brut, soit 36.103 milliards de dinars en 2024, 37.790 milliards en 2025 et un montant prévisionnel de plus de 42.000 milliards en 2026. M. Lebbou a expliqué que l’année 2011, prise comme année de référence pour le calcul du PIB, était « inadaptée » et qu'une autre année sera, de ce fait, choisie. « Passer en douceur, sans secousses » sociales Autre indicateur de la bonne marche vers l’édification d’une économie « résiliente face aux fluctuations de l'économie mondiale », Abdelmadjid Tebboune a cité le chiffre de 13.000 projets d’investissement concrets. Dans ce registre, le président a annoncé la concrétisation officielle du Guichet unique à partir du 1ᵉʳ janvier prochain. En attendant, Omar Rekkache, l'actuel directeur de l’AAPI, l'agence algérienne de promotion de l’investissement, sera maintenu pour mener la transition. Cette marche de l'Algérie vers une nouvelle économie ne se fera pas au détriment du citoyen et du volet social, s’est en outre engagé le président. Bien que « l’équation soit difficile », « nous essayons de passer en douceur, sans secousses », a-t-il indiqué, assurant que l’État ne se délestera pas de son caractère social. L’article Tebboune face aux patrons : discours apaisé et bilan satisfaisant de l’économie algérienne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Éruption de Goumeri W-8 : le gouvernement nigérien intensifie la réponse technique et environnementale…
items.description: Les ministres du Pétrole, M. Hamadou Tini, et de l’Environnement, le colonel Abdoulaye Maizama, se sont rendus ce matin sur le bloc pétrolier d’Agadem pour évaluer, sur place, l’évolution de la situation au puits Goumeri W-8, touché depuis le 25 septembre 2026 par une éruption de pétrole brut et de gaz. La visite vise à superviser le déploiement des équipes techniques et l’application des mesures conservatoires destinées à sécuriser la plateforme dégradée, contenir le flux d’hydrocarbures et limiter les impacts environnementaux sur les sols et les ressources environnantes. Selon le ministère du Pétrole, la fuite est partiellement contenue, mais l’éruption se poursuit avec une intensité réduite. Les deux membres du gouvernement sont accompagnés d’une équipe d’experts algériens de la Sonatrach, arrivés expressément pour apporter leur expertise dans la maîtrise de l’incident. Leur mission porte notamment sur l’évaluation technique du puits, l’analyse des risques liés à l’éruption, le renforcement des dispositifs de sécurisation de la plateforme et l’appui à la conception des opérations de contrôle du flux. Cette collaboration s’inscrit dans le cadre de la coopération technique algéro-nigérienne dans les hydrocarbures, fondée sur le partage d’expertise, le transfert de savoir-faire, la formation et le renforcement des capacités du personnel nigérien. L’Algérie avait réaffirmé, avant l’incident, sa disponibilité à accompagner le Niger dans ce secteur à travers Sonatrach et ses filiales. Les experts algériens devraient également contribuer à l’enquête indépendante annoncée par le gouvernement afin de déterminer les causes de l’éruption et d’établir les responsabilités. Le ministre du Pétrole, M. Hamadou Tini, et son homologue de l’Environnement sont accompagnés du gouverneur de la région de Diffa, le général de division Ibrahim Bagadoma, des autorités locales et des équipes techniques mobilisées sur le site. La coordination vise à assurer une réponse simultanée sur les plans opérationnel, environnemental et sécuritaire. Le gouvernement a par ailleurs indiqué que des mesures conservatoires et de contrôle concernant l’opérateur ont été engagées, tandis que les opérations de sécurisation du site se poursuivent de jour comme de nuit. items.title: Caveman Watches partners with Mfantsipim School for 150th anniversary
items.description: Ghanaian watch brand Caveman Watches has partnered with Mfantsipim School to mark the institution’s 150th anniversary, celebrating its history of academic excellence, leadership and service. The partnership brings together the Accra-based watchmaker and the Cape Coast school, which was established in 1876 and is marking 150 years of educating generations of students who have contributed to Ghana and beyond. In a press release dated October 14, 2026, Caveman Watches said the collaboration reflects a shared appreciation for heritage, precision, excellence and lasting impact. The company said it was pleased to be associated with the anniversary celebrations and the generations of students, alumni, educators and supporters who have contributed to Mfantsipim’s reputation. Caveman Watches Business Development Manager, Solomon Kwasi Affum, said the partnership reflected the company’s commitment to celebrating Ghanaian excellence. “We are honoured to partner with Mfantsipim as it celebrates 150 years of excellence and nation-building. This milestone is a testament to the power of education, character, and vision in shaping generations,” he said. He added that the company was proud to be associated with an institution whose influence had extended across generations. Chairman of the Mfantsipim 150th Anniversary Planning Committee, Capt. John B. Yamoah, said partnerships with Ghanaian brands provided an opportunity to honour the school’s heritage while looking to the future. He said the collaboration reflected a shared appreciation for quality, distinction and lasting value. The partnership also draws on Mfantsipim’s motto, “Dwen Hwe Kan” , which means “Think and Look Ahead”. Both organisations said the collaboration highlighted the role of partnerships between Ghanaian institutions and homegrown businesses in celebrating national heritage, promoting local enterprise and inspiring future generations. About Caveman Watches Caveman Watches is a Ghanaian watch brand founded by Anthony Mensah Dzamefe on December 12, 2018. The company designs and hand-assembles timepieces in Accra, combining watchmaking craftsmanship with contemporary African design. About Mfantsipim School Established in 1876, Mfantsipim is one of Ghana’s historic secondary schools. Its 150th anniversary celebrates its longstanding tradition of academic achievement, character formation and leadership development.

items.title: We’ll pursue GH¢15m defamation suit against Sammy Gyamfi to its logical conclusion – Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers
items.description: Lawyers for Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin say they will pursue his GH¢15 million defamation suit against Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi despite the High Court’s decision to set aside the case. The legal team says it is awaiting the full judgment delivered on October 14, 2026, before deciding on its next steps. In a statement issued by Dehyena Chambers, the lawyers said the court registry had not made a copy of the judgment available to them as of 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday. They confirmed that they had their client’s instructions to pursue the matter “to its logical conclusion”. The High Court, presided over by Justice Akwasi Adjenim Boateng, set aside the suit because the writ did not sufficiently specify the statements alleged to be defamatory. Read also: Sammy Gyamfi using ‘procedural roadblocks’ to dodge defamation case? – Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers The court ruled that the writ failed to meet the requirements of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47). The ruling was based on a procedural issue and did not determine whether Mr Gyamfi’s comments were defamatory. In the same statement, Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers accused Mr Gyamfi of relying on procedural issues rather than filing a defence to the suit. They said Mr Gyamfi’s lawyers, Ayine & Partners, had written to the court on August 26, 2026, confirming their authority to accept service of the writ on his behalf. According to the legal team, the law firm later returned the documents to the court registry, saying their client had changed his mind. They also alleged that a subsequent attempt to serve the documents personally on Mr Gyamfi at his office was unsuccessful. Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers argued that the rules of court recognise service as complete when a lawyer undertakes in writing to accept court documents on behalf of a client. The GH¢15 million suit arose from comments Mr Gyamfi made about Mr Afenyo-Markin during a JoyNews Newsfile programme in August 2026. The Minority Leader is seeking damages over the alleged defamatory remarks.

items.title: 3 000 milliards de FCFA non rapatriés, nigérisation au point mort : L’État tape du poing sur la table face aux pétroliers chinois…
items.description: Cinq mois après la signature du protocole d’accord du 18 mai 2026, le gouvernement nigérien a dressé un bilan sans concession de la coopération pétrolière avec ses partenaires chinois. Dans un communiqué officiel, lu le 13 octobre 2026 par le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Bakary Yaou Sangaré, Niamey dénonce des manquements financiers et contractuels majeurs et accorde 45 jours à la CNPC, WAPCO et la SORAZ pour se conformer aux engagements bilatéraux et communautaires. L’heure des comptes a sonné dans le secteur pétrolier nigérien. Réuni pour évaluer la mise en œuvre des 45 engagements issus du protocole de partenariat signé le 18 mai 2026, le comité de suivi gouvernemental a rendu public ses conclusions particulièrement sévères à l’encontre des sociétés chinoises opérant sur la chaîne pétrolière nationale : la CNPC, WAPCO et la raffinerie de Zinder (SORAZ). Plus de 3 000 milliards de FCFA hors du circuit financier national Au cœur des griefs formulés par les autorités nigériennes figure la question cruciale du rapatriement des recettes d’exportation du brut. Depuis le lancement des exportations en avril 2024, plus de 3 000 milliards de FCFA de recettes n’ont toujours pas été rapatriés au Niger par la CNPC. Alors que l’État a intégralement remboursé au 30 mars 2026, le prêt commercial de 400 millions de dollars contracté en 2024, seuls 105 milliards de FCFA sont effectivement revenus dans les caisses nationales. Ce taux dérisoire d’environ 6% contre une moyenne communautaire supérieure à 70% au sein de l’UEMOA a privé le Trésor public de près de 17,4 milliards de FCFA de recettes directes et asséché les liquidités des banques locales. Sur le plan juridique, Niamey a tenu à rappeler la primauté absolue de la réglementation des changes de l’UEMOA sur les anciennes conventions dérogatoires datant de 2008 et 2019. L’État exige l’application immédiate du mécanisme pérenne négocié avec la BCEAO, avertissant qu’en cas de refus persistant, les sanctions de l’institut d’émission communautaire seront appliquées sans réserve. Sous-traitance locale et nigérisation : des engagements restés lettre morte Le réquisitoire gouvernemental met également en lumière des défaillances flagrantes en matière de contenu local et de gestion des ressources humaines : Contenu local opaque : Les quotas contractuels fixés pour 2026 (20% pour la CNPC, 25% pour WAPCO et 56% pour la SORAZ) ne sont appuyés par aucun justificatif probant. Les déclarations transmises comportent des doublons et des montants pluriannuels non ventilés, tandis que la SORAZ n’a fourni aucun état d’exécution. Remplacement des expatriés au point mort : Aucun plan de nigérisation sur quatre ans n’a été déposé par les trois entreprises. Le processus de recrutement local censé pourvoir 558 postes occupés par des expatriés sur les champs pétroliers d’Agadem n’a jamais été amorcé. Audits RH bloqués : La SORAZ et WAPCO refusent toujours d’engager l’audit indépendant de leurs effectifs. Réserves non certifiées : Depuis 2008, les volumes des réserves pétrolières du bloc d’Agadem reposent sur les seules déclarations unilatérales de la CNPC, sans aucune certification par un cabinet d’audit indépendant. Sur le plan énergétique interne, la SORAZ tourne actuellement à un régime réduit de 15 000 barils/jour (soit 75% de sa capacité nominale de 20 000 b/j), alimentant des tensions sur l’approvisionnement du marché domestique en carburant. Face à ce constat, le gouvernement nigérien a formellement notifié une mise en demeure assortie d’un délai d’exécution strict de 45 jours aux trois directions générales. Celles-ci doivent sans délai transmettre des états financiers rectifiés, déposer leurs plans de nigérisation, lancer les recrutements et coopérer pleinement à la certification indépendante des réserves d’Agadem. « Le partenariat avec la Chine est ancien et l’État entend le poursuivre, mais sur la base de la transparence, du respect strict des engagements et de la défense intransigeante des intérêts du Niger », a conclu le chef de la diplomatie nigérienne. À l’expiration du préavis, Niamey se réserve le droit de tirer toutes les conséquences juridiques, contractuelles et souveraines qui s’imposent. Avec les partenaires chinois, il faut nécessairement user du bâton et de la carotte. Ils sont des partenaires sans scrupules et prêts à tout pour uniquement leurs intérêts. En cette ère de refondation, l’état doit être ferme. C’est cela la souveraineté. items.title: Martin Kpebu urges Afenyo-Markin not to return to court over Sammy Gyamfi lawsuit
items.description: Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has urged Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin not to return to court over his GH¢15 million defamation suit against Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi, following the dismissal of the case by the High Court. According to him, the two parties should resolve the matter amicably, arguing that continued litigation could undermine cooperation between the government and opposition Members of Parliament. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, Mr Kpebu said the dismissal of the suit meant there was no pending case preventing public discussion of the issues surrounding it. “Once the writ has been struck out, or the case has been dismissed, there’s nothing before the court, so there’s no risk at all. You discuss it, you’re free to,” he said. On Wednesday, October 14, the High Court’s General Jurisdiction 1 threw out Mr Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15 million defamation suit, ruling that the writ was incurably defective and incompetent and could not properly invoke the court’s jurisdiction. The court relied on Coleman v Newmont on the applicable procedural rule and Owusu Domena on the requirement to raise objections promptly. The ruling brought proceedings under the defective writ to an end but did not determine whether the statements complained of were defamatory. Mr Afenyo-Markin announced the lawsuit in Parliament on August 24, 2026, following allegations of extortion made against him amid a dispute involving GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. The suit named Mr Gyamfi and Multimedia Group Limited as defendants, with the Minority Leader maintaining that the allegations were false and intended to damage his reputation. The case also generated disagreement over service of the writ. Mr Gyamfi authorised his lawyers, Ayine & Partners, to accept the court documents, while Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers later said service had been completed and rejected claims that their client was avoiding it. Responding to a question on whether the media could continue reporting on the controversy without risking contempt of court or breaching an injunction, Mr Kpebu said there was no legal impediment he was aware of following the dismissal of the suit. He, however, cautioned that media discussions could still expose individuals to fresh legal action if they involved defamatory statements. “Except, of course, if in discussing it, maybe certain statements are made which are defamatory, then I think Afenyo-Markin deserves the right to sue again,” he said. Read also: High Court throws out Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15m defamation suit against Sammy Gyamfi Despite this, Mr Kpebu urged the Minority Leader not to return to court over the existing dispute, calling for an amicable resolution. “I also believe he shouldn’t go. I think he shouldn’t go back to court,” he added. Mr Kpebu argued that litigation of this nature could strain relations between the government and opposition lawmakers, particularly when both sides continued to engage in public business despite their political differences. He said successive governments had supported opposition MPs in various ways, including through development projects such as road construction in their constituencies. “It’s not just this government. For as long as I’ve been politically aware, government often engages opposition MPs and tries to support them,” he said. He maintained that such engagements were not unusual in Ghana’s political system and questioned the sustainability of pursuing legal action while the government and opposition continued to cooperate on other matters.

items.title: Vinícius handed four-match ban, to miss Real Madrid’s Clasico against Barcelona
items.description: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Júnior has been handed a four-match suspension after pulling an opponent’s hair during his side’s 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday. The Brazilian was sent off in the 73rd minute after grabbing and tugging the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba as the two players sprinted down the pitch. Vinícius had scored moments earlier, but the goal was ruled out. The Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee announced the suspension shortly before Real Madrid’s Champions League match against Roma on Wednesday. According to the committee, Vinícius received a two-match ban for the hair-pulling incident and an additional two matches for his aggressive reaction to the referee after being shown the red card. Referee Isidro Díaz de Mera stated in his match report that the forward protested the decision by raising his voice and approaching him aggressively, adding that Vinícius had to be restrained by his teammates. The suspension means Vinícius will miss Real Madrid’s home fixture against Sevilla on Sunday and their trip to Barcelona the following week for the highly anticipated Clasico. He will also be unavailable for Madrid’s away matches against Racing Santander and Valencia. The four-match ban comes as a setback for Real Madrid, who will be without one of their key attacking players for several important domestic fixtures. items.title: Réfugiés sahraouis : à Genève, l’Algérie recadre sèchement le Maroc
items.description: L’Algérie a réitéré, mardi soir, son plaidoyer en faveur du maintien de l’aide et de la protection des réfugiés sahraouis , conformément aux obligations et aux engagements consacrés par la Convention de 1951 relative au statut des réfugiés. Dans une allocution prononcée à l’occasion de la 77e session du Comité exécutif du Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), à Genève, le représentant permanent de l’Algérie, Idris Latreche, s’adressant au Haut-Commissaire, a estimé que l’attention portée aux réfugiés sahraouis ne devait toutefois pas occulter le processus politique visant à s’attaquer aux causes profondes de leur situation. « Comme vous l’avez souligné à juste titre, les engagements consacrés par cette convention doivent rester en vigueur. Ils doivent le rester parce que l’aide et la protection internationales ne relèvent pas de la charité, mais constituent des droits fondamentaux et intrinsèques des réfugiés, tant que les causes profondes des déplacements forcés qui les ont contraints à chercher refuge n’ont pas été traitées », a affirmé le diplomate algérien. Situation des réfugiés sahraouis : l’Algérie appelle à traiter les « causes profondes » « Cette analyse s’applique pleinement à la situation actuelle des réfugiés sahraouis. Si le regain d’intérêt pour leurs souffrances, à ce stade précis, est une évolution bienvenue, cette attention ne doit pas occulter le processus politique chargé de s’attaquer aux causes profondes de cette situation », a-t-il insisté. En tant que pays d’accueil des réfugiés sahraouis depuis plus de cinq décennies et principal contributeur financier à l’amélioration de leurs conditions de vie, l’Algérie appelle la communauté internationale à maintenir et à renforcer son soutien à ces populations contraintes de fuir leur territoire et la colonisation marocaine. Réfugiés sahraouis : les trois vérités de l’Algérie Toutefois, aux yeux d’Alger, toute initiative concernant cette question doit s’appuyer rigoureusement sur les « réalités » du terrain et, surtout, sur trois faits qu’elle considère comme incontestables. La première vérité concerne la spécificité de la situation des réfugiés sahraouis. « Ceux-ci ne sont pas des réfugiés ayant fui la précarité économique, des conditions climatiques extrêmes ou des guerres civiles internes, mais des personnes déplacées d’un territoire non autonome appelé Sahara occidental . Leur droit inaliénable à l’autodétermination demeure au cœur même de leur détresse », a souligné le représentant de l’Algérie. La deuxième vérité réside dans le fait que la volonté des réfugiés des camps sahraouis de Tindouf a toujours constitué, et constitue encore, le principe de référence auquel tous doivent se conformer, selon lui. « Les camps sont ouverts et se caractérisent par leur transparence. Ils accueillent de manière permanente plus de cinq entités des Nations Unies et plus de vingt organisations internationales non gouvernementales. Ils reçoivent également des visites régulières de donateurs internationaux, d’observateurs internationaux et de différents mécanismes des Nations Unies », a-t-il affirmé. Enfin, la troisième et dernière vérité assénée par le diplomate algérien concerne les principes fondamentaux de l’action humanitaire. « Même si cela peut sembler relever de l’évidence, je suis fermement convaincu de la nécessité de le rappeler encore et encore : l’aide humanitaire ne doit pas être instrumentalisée à des fins politiques ni servir d’outil de pression politique. La souffrance des réfugiés sahraouis ne doit pas non plus devenir une monnaie d’échange permettant de marquer des points politiques ou de poursuivre des objectifs étroits et égoïstes », a insisté M. Latrèche. On l’aura compris : il s’agit d’une réponse directe du représentant de l’Algérie à son homologue marocain, qui avait plutôt invité les bailleurs de fonds et les Nations Unies à réorienter l’aide humanitaire vers des solutions durables pour les populations des camps de Tindouf. Le représentant marocain préconise rien de moins que le rapatriement librement consenti, l’intégration locale ou la réinstallation, afin de mettre fin à un statu quo de plus de cinquante ans. « À la lumière de ces réalités fondamentales, cette délégation estime, avec une profonde conviction, qu’il faut éviter d’envoyer un message erroné au mauvais moment. Nous devons également éviter le risque de brouiller les distinctions entre les impératifs humanitaires et les réalités politiques », a estimé Idris Latrèche. « Enfin, nous devons nous abstenir de susciter toute confusion susceptible d’aggraver davantage les souffrances des réfugiés sahraouis, au lieu de leur apporter l’aide à laquelle ils ont pleinement droit », a-t-il complété. Réfugiés sahraouis : à Genève, Idris Latreche corrige la délégation marocaine Le diplomate algérien n’a pas manqué de critiquer vertement la position marocaine, estimant que la partie qu’il tient pour responsable de la situation au Sahara occidental ne saurait prétendre donner des leçons sur les solutions durables. « Il est profondément regrettable, voire surprenant, de voir la partie qui porte la responsabilité première et entière de cette situation tenter de donner des leçons à cet honorable comité sur les solutions durables. Passer du déni absolu à la prétention de détenir une autorité morale dont on se pose soi-même en garant… voilà ce que nous appelons de l’opportunisme dans sa pire expression. En réponse, je tiens à affirmer que la communauté internationale n’est pas aveugle aux faits et qu’elle n’ignore pas les racines de cette situation », a conclu Idris Latreche. items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.20 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.17
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.20 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.17 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.65 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 15 (Thursday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.
