items.title: Omani FM meets PM Shehbaz, commends Pakistan's 'sustained diplomatic efforts' for regional peace
items.description: Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday and appreciated Pakistan’s “sustained diplomatic efforts” for de-escalation and peaceful solutions to regional challenges, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. Both Pakistan and Oman have been engaged in efforts for de-escalation after US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February resulted in a conflict that has now expanded further into the Middle East. Albusaidi’s meeting with PM Shehbaz was held on the second day of his two-day trip to Pakistan, during which he also attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) and held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. In his meeting with the Omani foreign minister, PM Shehbaz “highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to-people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship”, the PMO statement said. The premier underscored that Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region, it added. “The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission. “He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries,” the statement said. It further stated that PM Shehbaz “noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues”. He appreciated Oman’s “principled stance” of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes, the statement said. For his part, Albusaidi thanked the government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and “expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC session”, the PMO statement said. It added that the Omani foreign minister “agreed that it (JMC session) would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit”. “The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges,” the statement read. It added that PM Shehbaz also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman JMC, as well as agreements and memoranda of understanding for bilateral cooperation between the two sides in the areas of media cooperation, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology and facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges. ‘Totally unacceptable’ Earlier in the day, Albusaidi held a joint press conference with Deputy PM Dar, during which the latter said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”. At the outset of the press conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission. He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports. “Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told the media. He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan. The ministers discussed the situation in the Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”. Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks. “I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said. “I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said. They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said. DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”. “This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said. Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries. “Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said. He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war . He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”. The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question. “We are both on the same page,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement. Responding to a question about the gaps in bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between the US and Iran. Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”. Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”. JMC session The meeting of the commission was co-chaired by Dar and Albusaidi. The two sides “reaffirmed their close fraternal ties and commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, maritime and logistics connectivity, agriculture, industry, energy, workforce mobility, human resource development, education, IT, media and climate change, among other areas”, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Both ministers emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties, facilitating workforce mobility, and promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration. FM Dar stressed the need for “timely implementation of agreed outcomes through close institutional coordination and sustained engagement between joint working group meetings”, the statement added. According to FO, the Oman FM thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality, appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and security, and reaffirmed Muscat’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two countries. Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace Speaking at the outset of the JMC session, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting. Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East. “I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”. “We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said. He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities. Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings. He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”. Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandab and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues. He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.” Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries. “I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said. He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers. “We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said. He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region. “Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US. Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security. “The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said. He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries. “Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation. According to a joint statement, the two sides agreed to hold the ninth session of the JMC next year. After the session concluded, Albusaidi posted on that he had a “constructive day” in Islamabad co-chairing JMC session with Dar. “We reviewed practical ways to deepen our longstanding partnership in trade, investment, energy, logistics and other priority areas, and agreed on closer follow-up to turn opportunities into results,” he said, expressing gratitude for the “warm hospitality and the shared commitment to cooperation and regional dialogue”. Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement Earlier in the day, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, FO said. The visiting dignitary had arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit. The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to FO. “The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability,” FO said. Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added. A day earlier, FO said the JMC session would review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation. The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation”.

items.title: Pakistani, Chinese armies begin joint training exercise in Xinjiang
items.description: GILGIT: A joint training exercise of Pakistani and Chinese armies, “Karakoram 2026”, began in the Xinjiang province of China on Wednesday. The opening ceremony of Karakoram 2026 was held at a training base in Korla city, according to the China Military Bugle, the official media account of Beijing’s armed forces. The two sides exchanged counter-terrorism experience and Pakistani troops observed some Chinese weapons and equipment. Before the drill commenced, Colonel Chen Xi, the press secretary of China’s defence ministry, said last week that the exercise would help the two sides deepen exchanges and cooperation and enhance their ability to jointly respond to the threat of terrorism. He said the training would focus on “joint anti-terrorism clearance operations at high altitudes”. The press secretary added that the drills would involve drone operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and would cover “joint command and live-force exercises”, according to China’s Xinhua news agency. Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership. In September, the two countries held a joint patrolling exercise at Mantika Pass, at an altitude of approximately 4,700 metres, near Khunjerab top situated in the upper area of GB’s Hunza. In May, they reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral military cooperation and strategic coordination. Additional input from Anadolu Agency

items.title: Pope out of bed, progress ‘normal’ after cancer operation
items.description: Pope Leo XIV is out of bed, walking and eating after doctors removed a cancerous tumour from his lung, while post-surgery tests show his progress is “normal”, his doctors said Wednesday. Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is now awaiting the results of a biopsy to determine if the cancer has spread. Blood tests and a chest X-ray meanwhile “confirm a normal post-operative course”, doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora said in a statement released by the Vatican. “The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed,” they said. The discovery on Tuesday that a nodule detected in Leo’s lung was cancerous has plunged the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty. “It’s a shock for everyone. We’re in ‘wait-and-see’ mode,” a Vatican source told AFP. Doctors said his recovery was “proceeding as expected” and the pontiff had eaten both breakfast and lunch, been walking about his room, and had done some respiratory physiotherapy. Another Vatican source said the pope had even celebrated a mass on Wednesday in a specially prepared room on the 10th floor of the hospital, where is staying. The papal suite on the same floor is where popes are usually treated. It has a private chapel but is currently being refurbished. – ‘Show my spiritual support’ – The sporty 71-year-old, elected as the first pope from the United States only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers. Messages of support flooded in from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles III, who is also being treated for an undisclosed cancer. A banner flying outside the hospital read “Long live the pope!” and a handful of people recited prayers for the hospitalised pontiff. Nearby, nun Angele Bilegue said she had come to pray for Leo. “I’m not worried. I came to express my closeness, to show my spiritual support, because I also came for Pope Francis,” she told AFP. Leo’s predecessor, the Argentine Francis, spent five weeks last year being treated for double pneumonia at the same hospital, before his death at the Vatican on April 21, 2025. Experts said much would depend on how advanced Leo’s cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it had been detected early and was localised. Before the operation, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery should take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20. “If we are dealing with stage I or II disease, and recovery is good… the patient can resume a normal life and usual activities within a few weeks,” Alain Gelibter, an oncologist at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, told AFP. The Chicago-born Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday. In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation. – New uncertainty – The shock news of the tennis-playing pope’s illness has rattled the Catholic Church. Expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP: “The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy.” Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, told AFP “we have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic. Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image.” His health issues may prompt him to speed up personnel appointments, Munsterman said. Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”. Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, newly nominated to the influential role of dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrated mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday instead of Leo. The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades. items.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3 in Champions League
items.description: Bradley Barcola silenced his critics as the Liverpool forward ended his goal drought with a hat-trick in a chaotic 6-3 win against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday. Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million ($161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August. But the France forward finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance. Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club. Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble. There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game. It was a welcome boost for Iraola following his first defeat in eight games as Liverpool manager when Premier League leaders Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday. Iraola this week said he has “100 per cent” trust in Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who has struggled mightily since joining from Bayer Leverkusen last year. Injuries to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, who all missed the trip to Austria, increased the pressure on Wirtz and Barcola to carry the Liverpool attack. The pair repaid Iraola’s faith with a much-needed display of their undoubted qualities. Now Iraola will demand they produce that level of intensity and quality on a regular basis. The trip to Linz was the second of six games in 18 days for Liverpool, forcing Iraola to make changes in a bid to save his players from burnout. Reds captain Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz were all rested as Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha came in. – Clinical Barcola – After some disjointed displays at the start of Iraola’s reign, this was an indication of what they can become under the former Bournemouth boss, although he will still be concerned about their defensive issues. Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, rising highest to meet Tsimikas’s corner with a thumping header past LASK keeper Lukas Jungwirth. The on-loan Barcelona defender’s goal was swiftly followed by one for Barcola 96 seconds later. Ngumoha was the catalyst with an incisive run into the LASK area and Barcola applied the finishing touch as he guided a clinical finish beyond Jungwirth. Iraola’s men were running riot and Barcola scored their third in the 37th minute. It was a riposte to the criticism of Wirtz and Barcola as the pair combined to cut through the LASK defence. Barcola picked out Wirtz and the German played a pinpoint return pass that allowed the 24-year-old to fire past Jungwirth. Frimpong has also frustrated Liverpool fans since signing last year, making his goal in the 51st minute a welcome tonic for the Dutch right-back. Tsimikas got to the byline and lofted a cross towards Frimpong, who belied his diminutive stature with a towering header into the bottom corner. Robert Ljubicic reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute with a composed finish from Yvan Dibango’s pass. But Barcola sealed his treble with a nimble finish from Frimpong’s pass in the 66th minute. Teed up by Frimpong, Koumas hit Liverpool’s sixth with a searing strike in the 72nd minute. Despite the introduction of Van Dijk and fellow defender Joe Gomez, Liverpool lost control in the closing stages. Florian Flecker’s diving header two minutes later punished slack Liverpool defending. Flecker struck again with a close-range finish in the 77th minute, but nothing could spoil Barcola’s big night. items.title: GRA submits preliminary report on drug shipment case to Mahama – Commissioner-General
items.description: The Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, has disclosed that a preliminary investigation report into the recent drug shipment case involving containers that left Ghana has been submitted to President John Dramani Mahama. He said the Authority was also working with the relevant security agencies to establish the full details of the incident and support efforts to address the concerns surrounding the shipment. Mr Sarpong made the disclosure when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), in response to concerns about the reputational damage the drug-related cases could cause Ghana. The question was raised by the Member of Parliament for Mpraeso and Vice-Chairperson of the Committee, Davis Ansah Opoku, who sought clarity on measures being taken to address the situation. Mr Sarpong described drug trafficking as a serious concern for the GRA and called for collective efforts to prevent the country from being used as a transit point for narcotics. He also revealed that the Authority regularly intercepts drugs and arrests suspected traffickers at the country’s entry and exit points, although such operations are not always made public. According to him, publicising every interception could alert drug traffickers and allow them to devise new methods to evade detection. Meanwhile, the GRA has urged taxpayers to take advantage of tax reliefs available under the law, saying many eligible individuals are missing out because of limited awareness. Mr Sarpong said the Authority was intensifying public education to ensure taxpayers understood the reliefs available to them under the Revenue Administration framework and the relevant tax laws, including the Income Tax Act, 2015 (Act 896). He said the GRA was committed to helping eligible taxpayers access the benefits provided by law and was working to improve awareness of the applicable requirements. The Commissioner-General also addressed issues relating to online cross-border transactions and attempts by some financial institutions to impose additional percentage charges on products. He explained that consumers were already paying the applicable 20 per cent charge but were not always aware of it, adding that the Authority was seeking to formalise the arrangement.

items.title: Man United line up three-man shortlist as sack looms for Michael Carrick
items.description: Manchester United are reportedly considering Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for Michael Carrick if the club decides to part ways with its current manager. According to talkSPORT, the three managers have attracted interest from different figures within the Old Trafford hierarchy as pressure mounts on Carrick following a difficult run of results. United’s reported interest comes after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, which extended their winless run to five matches across all competitions. The result also followed a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, a run of form that has raised concerns about the team’s performances and Carrick’s tactical decisions. The defeat to Atletico also prompted defender Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox over what he reportedly viewed as insufficient squad strengthening. United will look to end their poor run when they face historic rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday. Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, the station’s chief live football anchor, Adrian Durham, suggested Carrick’s position could become increasingly difficult if the team fails to improve. “Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go,” Durham said. He added that Carrick would need to turn around the team’s results to improve his chances of remaining in the job. Durham also expressed concerns about Carrick’s tactical decisions in the Atletico Madrid match, arguing that some of the changes made during the game contributed to United’s defeat. Among the three reported candidates, Nagelsmann and Conte are said to be available for an immediate appointment. Conte left Napoli by mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann reportedly departed his position as Germany coach following the country’s elimination by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup. The report said United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, was advocating for Nagelsmann internally as a potential successor should the club decide to dismiss Carrick. Hurzeler, meanwhile, remains under contract with Brighton until 2029 after signing an extension in May. The German coach is reportedly favoured by Wilcox and has overseen a strong start to the Premier League season, with Brighton winning four of their opening six matches to sit third in the standings. Hurzeler has also guided Brighton to victory over Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup in September, adding to his credentials as a potential candidate. However, Manchester United have not been reported to have made a formal appointment decision, and Carrick’s immediate future could depend on the team’s results in the coming matches. items.title: Sammy Gyamfi using ‘procedural roadblocks’ to dodge defamation case? – Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers
items.description: Lawyers for Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin have accused Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi of using procedural tactics to avoid responding to their client’s GH¢15 million defamation suit. The accusation comes after the High Court in Accra set aside the suit on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, ruling that the writ of summons did not sufficiently specify the statements alleged to be defamatory. In a statement, Mr Afenyo-Markin’s legal team questioned why Mr Gyamfi had allegedly focused on procedural issues instead of filing a defence to the allegations. The lawyers said Mr Gyamfi’s legal representatives, Ayine & Partners, had written to the court on August 26 confirming their authority to accept service of the writ on his behalf. They said the court bailiff subsequently served the documents on the law firm, but the lawyers returned them to the court registry the following day, indicating that their client had changed his mind. According to Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers, a subsequent attempt to serve the documents personally on Mr Gyamfi at his office was unsuccessful, with the GoldBod CEO allegedly refusing to accept them. The legal team argued that under the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), service should be considered complete once a lawyer has undertaken in writing to accept court documents on behalf of a client. Read also: We’ll pursue GH¢15m defamation suit against Sammy Gyamfi to its logical conclusion – Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers However, the High Court, presided over by Justice Akwasi Agyenim Boateng, ruled that the writ was defective because it failed to sufficiently particularise the alleged defamatory statements, as required under Order 57, Rule 2 of C.I. 47. The ruling addressed the procedural requirements for filing a defamation case and did not determine whether Mr Gyamfi’s comments were defamatory. Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers have criticised the decision, arguing that procedural irregularities should not be allowed to undermine substantive justice. They said they were yet to receive a copy of the court’s ruling as of 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday and would determine their next steps after reviewing it. The lawyers added that they had instructions from their client to pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. The dispute followed comments made by Mr Gyamfi on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme in August 2026, during which he described Mr Afenyo-Markin as an “extortionist” amid a public debate over the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. Mr Afenyo-Markin subsequently sued Mr Gyamfi and Multimedia Group Limited, the parent company of JoyNews, seeking GH¢15 million in damages, a retraction, an apology and a permanent injunction against further publication of the alleged defamatory statements.

items.title: You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over what he described as disrespectful comments about President Bola Tinubu, saying anyone seeking the presidency must show discipline and respect for public institutions. Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election. In his remarks, Shettima said Atiku’s repeated presidential bids and recent policy proposals did not, in his view, excuse language he considered disrespectful toward the sitting president. He also questioned how Atiku’s proposed production subsidies would be funded. “Those who want equity must come with clean hands. You can call him Bola. If you like, you can call him Adekunle. But the truth is that he is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Atiku Abubakar. I will still respect him and call him his former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar. “I will not follow suit with the maverick Babachir Lawal and call him Kachalla, no. But believe me, Atiku Abubakar, who has contested for the presidency of this country for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of Oginga Odinga.” Shettima framed his criticism as an argument about the conduct expected of presidential contenders, saying the higher the office sought, the greater the responsibility candidates bear in their words and dealings with public institutions. “The presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is not an ordinary political prize. It is the highest expression of constitutional authority in our country. And those who aspire to occupy it must demonstrate, even before they get there, the qualities they will expect of themselves, if entrusted with the responsibility of leading more than 200 million Nigerians. “Political ambition is not merely the desire to occupy public office. It is a test of character, cerebral strength, intellectual maturity, and responsibility. The higher the office a person seeks, the greater the discipline expected in his words, conduct, and relationship with public institutions,” he added. Turning to Atiku’s proposal on production subsidies, Shettima questioned the cost and the competing priorities that might be affected. “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, this political season has become a masterclass in cinematic comedy. Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal for production subsidies raises questions that some changes cannot answer. Who pays? Who benefits? And which competing priorities must surrender their funding? A change in ideological wardrobe cannot balance a national budget.” The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election. The post You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The illusion of a good deal: Why some everyday money-saving habits may be costing you more
items.description: At a busy filling station somewhere in Accra, an attendant rests the pump nozzle inside a sedan’s fuel tank. Seconds after a sharp metallic click signals the tank is full, the attendant glances at the driver and asks a routine question: “Master, should I round it up?” With a nod from the driver, the attendant squeezes the lever again, forcing several more liters into the tank. Across Ghana’s consumer marketplace, from fuel stations and Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) refill depots to auto parts hubs like Abossey Okai, a collection of deeply ingrained urban myths dictates everyday commercial choices. Driven by a desire to maximize value or outsmart perceived commercial inefficiencies, consumers routinely embrace practices that promise more for less. Yet, an examination of these widespread consumer habits reveals a stark economic reality: the short-term illusion of getting extra value almost always ends in severe long-term financial loss, safety risks, and market inefficiency. The True Cost of ‘Topping Off’: LPG Cylinders and Fuel Tanks The practice of topping off isn’t confined to gasoline. At residential LPG stations, consumers frequently request that gas cylinders be filled to ‘full’—demanding that attendants bypass manufacturer safety thresholds to cram in maximum volume. The technical risks of overfilling liquefied gas and liquid fuel are well-documented. Examining the true cost of topping off highlights significant hidden long-term consequences associated with common consumer actions. For instance, forcing fuel past the first click floods the EVAP charcoal canister with liquid fuel, ultimately triggering expensive engine repairs. Similarly, overfilling domestic LPG cylinders beyond specification eliminates the twenty percent thermal expansion buffer, substantially increasing the risk of catastrophic valve failure. The ‘Tested’ Illusion: Second-Hand Parts vs. New Imports When it comes to cars and home appliances, many people truly believe that “home-used” or imported second-hand items are automatically better than brand-new ones. In places like Accra and Kumasi, mechanics almost always advise car owners to buy used original parts taken from old imported cars rather than new spare parts. Their reason? They say the used part is “tested and proven.” While original parts are usually better than cheap knockoffs, buying someone else’s discarded junk comes with serious hidden risks. First, hidden wear and tear presents a major issue: a used shock absorber or brake part might look fine on the outside, but it could easily have invisible cracks or worn-out internal rubber from old accidents, age, or weather exposure. Second, there is a distinct lack of guarantees or warranties, as second-hand items almost never come with a real warranty compared to brand-new parts. If a used alternator dies three weeks after installation, the consumer must pay for another part and pay the mechanic all over again. Finally, high power bills pose a major financial strain; sellers of used fridges and appliances often argue that older imported models are built stronger than new ones, yet these old motors consume far more electricity, rapidly eating up any upfront savings through sky-high monthly power bills. Transit Chaos: The Economics of the Pre-Stop The psychological compulsion to gain a brief advantage extends to public transportation. Drivers of trotros—the commercial minibuses that form the backbone of urban transport—frequently drop off or pick up passengers dozens of meters before designated bus stops. While drivers view early stops as a quick tactic to beat competing minibuses to the curb, the aggregate economic impact is negative. This premature stopping leads to micro-congestion, as trailing vehicles are forced to brake unexpectedly or maneuver around stationary buses, creating severe bottleneck gridlock along key corridors like the George Walker Bush Highway. Consequently, commuters suffer a substantial loss of productive hours, losing cumulative time weekly in artificially created traffic jams that diminish urban productivity across commercial centers. Furthermore, pedestrian risks escalate drastically when disembarking passengers outside designated zones are forced to navigate active traffic lanes. An Imperative for Behavioral Change Ghana’s consumer practices are rooted in an understandable attempt to manage costs within a demanding economic landscape. However, the reliance on informal heuristics over technical specifications creates systemic waste. Moving toward a more efficient market requires deliberate shifts in both policy and consumer behavior. To achieve this, consumers must respect manufacturer protocols by treating equipment limits—whether fuel nozzle clicks or LPG weight markers, as engineered safety limits rather than arbitrary guidelines. In addition, vehicle and appliance owners should prioritize total cost of ownership, evaluating purchases by their full lifecycle costs, including energy efficiency, durability, and warranty protections, rather than initial purchase price alone. Finally, municipal assemblies and driver unions must enforce transit discipline, prioritizing organized boarding at designated stops to protect city mobility and safety. True consumer value is not found in pushing equipment past its engineered limits or opting for worn-out hardware. Recognizing the hidden economic costs of these popular myths is the first step toward building a safer, more sustainable marketplace. About the author; William Wallace Tamakloe is an Associate PR Director at Touchpoint Magna Carta.

items.title: AES-CEDEAO: les experts de la Task force préparent la participation de l’AES au prochain round des négociations
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 14 octobre 2026) En prélude à la prochaine rencontre de négociations entre la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) et la Commission économique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO) qui se tiendra dans les jours à venir à Dakar au Sénégal, les hauts fonctionnaires réunis au sein de la Task force confédérale, se sont réunis ce 14 octobre dans la capitale burkinabè, pour préparer la participation des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’espace confédéral à ce cadre de dialogue. Les membres de la Task force réunissant les experts du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso vont, au cours de cette réunion, identifier les axes et questions prioritaires consacrant la position des pays membres de l’AES lors des négociations. Les conclusions de leur travaux seront examinées par les ministres en charge des Affaires étrangères de la Confédération AES, et serviront de boussole aux négociations avec la CEDEAO, selon le chef de la délégation malienne, l’Ambassadeur Amadou MAÏGA. « Les domaines tels que la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, le commerce, l'intégration des peuples et les questions diplomatiques et institutionnelles, sont entre autres points qui devront faire l’objet d’échanges à cette réunion préliminaire à la rencontre des Chefs de la diplomatie de l’AES », a-t-il indiqué. Félicitant l’AES et la CEDEAO, animées selon lui, d’un même esprit, celui de la préservation de l’intérêt des populations de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, le chef de la délégation du Niger l’Ambassadeur Ousmane ALHASSANE, a salué la mise en place effective de la Task force qui va œuvrer à l’harmonisation de la feuille de route des consultations et des négociations de Dakar. « Ce rendez-vous engage l'avenir des relations entre deux espaces que l'histoire, la géographie, les échanges et les peuples continuent de relier. Notre responsabilité est donc de préparer une position rigoureuse, cohérente et pleinement conforme aux orientations du Collège des Chefs d'État de notre Confédération », précise le chef de la délégation burkinabè, l’Ambassadeur Yirigouin Hermann TOE, par ailleurs Secrétaire général du ministère des Affaires étrangères. Pour lui, l’enjeu de ces échanges est de mutualiser les forces qui permettront à terme de construire une intégration adaptée aux aspirations des peuples des deux espaces sous régionales. Présidant la cérémonie d’ouverture, le chef de la délégation du Burkina Faso a appelé les experts à des échanges fructueux, favorisant une lecture et une compréhension mutuelles des enjeux et de tous les contours des dispositions qui seront soumises à la négociation. Avant l’étape de Dakar, les ministres des Affaires étrangères du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso, vont se réunir à leur tour, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, pour examiner les conclusions et les recommandations de cette réunion des experts de la Task force de négociations. DCRP/MAE L’article AES-CEDEAO: les experts de la Task force préparent la participation de l’AES au prochain round des négociations est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Family seeks autopsy, police investigation into death of student 12 days after Abomosu SHS enrolment
items.description: The family of a 14-year-old student who died 12 days after enrolling at Abomosu STEM Senior High School in the Eastern Region is demanding a thorough police investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. Daniel Boateng Mintah died on September 30, 2026, less than two weeks after leaving home to begin senior high school. The family says conflicting accounts of the events leading to his death, questions about medication found among his belongings and concerns over the condition of his body at the mortuary have raised questions that require urgent investigation. According to the family, Daniel’s mother, Joyce Mintah, spoke to him earlier on the day he died before they received a call informing them that he was unwell and needed an injection for suspected malaria. The family says they were asked to send GH¢50 for the injection and provide his National Health Insurance Scheme details. However, subsequent attempts to obtain updates on his condition were unsuccessful for several hours, leaving them without clear information about his situation. At about 3:10 p.m., a caller who identified himself as the school’s headmaster asked Daniel’s parents to report to the school urgently. They immediately set off but were later redirected to Kwabeng Hospital, where they were informed that their son had been brought in dead. Daniel’s father, David Mintah, said a doctor informed the family that the boy had died before arriving at the hospital and recommended a post-mortem examination to establish the cause of death. The family’s concerns have since extended to the condition of Daniel’s body. Mr Mintah claims he found the body bleeding when he visited the Tafo mortuary on October 6. The body had been transferred from Kwabeng Hospital to the mortuary on October 1 at the family’s request. The family is also seeking clarification over reports that Daniel left the school’s orientation area to urinate but failed to return. They want investigators to establish the events between his last reported activities at school and the circumstances under which he was taken to the hospital. Daniel’s elder sister, Vivian Mintah, a nurse, has separately raised questions about psychiatric medication reportedly found among his belongings handed over by the school. She is seeking an explanation from the school regarding the medication, including how it came to be among his possessions and whether it had been prescribed to him. The family has appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno, and the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, to intervene and ensure a comprehensive investigation into the matter. It is also calling for Daniel’s body to be transferred to the Police Hospital in Accra to facilitate further investigations and help establish the cause of death. The family says it wants answers to the questions surrounding the teenager’s death and clarity on the events leading to the loss of their son.

items.title: Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing
items.description: In the aftermath of the bombing of a mine in the Halayeb Triangle that left scores of Sudanese miners dead, Egypt and Sudan are discussing a new security framework along the countries’ shared eastern border. That framework would provide for joint coordination to pursue what both sides regard as security risks arising from organized crime, Sudanese and Egyptian officials told Mada Masr. The push toward closer coordination comes amid public outcry in Sudan and diplomatic concern in international quarters over the killing of scores of artisanal miners in the disputed Halayeb Triangle on Saturday. That public outcry was accentuated on Monday when a gunman killed two Egyptians in a main market in southern Khartoum in what Sudanese security officials involved in the investigations told Mada Masr was a retaliatory attack. The shooting took place at around 2 pm near the Export Development Bank in the Local Market , a security source in Khartoum State police told Mada Masr. Three Egyptians were targeted in the market’s commercial area. Two died at the scene, while the third was taken to the Omdurman Medical Corps Hospital for treatment. Ali al-Laouta, a vegetable seller at the market, witnessed Monday’s shooting. He told Mada Masr that he noticed a man wearing a military uniform bearing the badge of the joint force of military-allied armed movements buying some items in the market. He then suddenly pointed his weapon at the three Egyptians shopping nearby, opened fire and fled the scene, Laouta adds. Police patrols and security units responded to the scene and tracked down the suspect, a source in the Khartoum police’s criminal investigations department told Mada Masr. The suspect initially resisted arrest, opening fire on security forces, but officers eventually subdued him, seized the weapon used in the attack and took him into custody, the source said. One member of the arrest unit was shot in the leg during the exchange of fire, a security officer involved in the operation said. The injured officer was hospitalized and is in stable condition, he added. The suspect is a member of the “support forces” — a wide range of armed formations that fight alongside the Sudanese military in the current war — a source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr. Sudan’s military-led government adopted a wartime policy that put the joint force, its main battlefield ally, in charge of protecting state institutions and supporting security operations in cities under military control. That has left the alliance with a heavy presence in urban areas. But a string of violent incidents involving joint force members in recent months has stoked public concerns and prompted authorities to review the policy and seek to curb the allied group’s urban presence. The source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr that the suspect was subjected to intensive questioning about his military affiliation and how he had obtained the weapon used in the attack. The interrogating officer told Mada Masr that, in his initial statement, the suspect said he had shot the Egyptian men in retaliation for his brother’s death in Saturday’s strikes. The shooting comes amid a wave of polarization in Sudanese public opinion following the deadly airstrike near the Sudanese-Egyptian border that killed scores of Sudanese people. The shooting adds more complexity to an already charged public sphere. Sudanese lawyer Oweis Salah Eddin al-Iraqi urged authorities to disclose the facts related to the miners’ deaths directly to the public, saying the case had become a matter of public concern and that any mishandling could provoke backlash. Many in the public and political arena are viewing the shooting in the context of wider accountability for the miners’ deaths. Viewing the market shooting in isolation from the attack on the miners would offer an incomplete assessment of the situation, said Adel Ibrahim Hamad, the head of Sudan’s Ashigga Party. The party was re-established by former members of the Democratic Unionist Party, drawing inspiration from an earlier party of the same name that called for union with Egypt. The revived party focuses on national issues, paying particular attention to Sudanese-Egyptian relations. Discussion of Monday’s shooting, Hamad argued, must begin with the original incident, saying Egypt’s response was disproportionate to the violation, “if any.” “Approaching the discussion from any other angle, such as platitudes about the strategic relationship [between the two countries] and the need to prevent an isolated incident from affecting it, would distract from a recurring Egyptian failing in handling Sudanese issues,” he said. For journalist Majed Mohamed Ali, Sudanese authorities have seriously underestimated the political and security consequences, at an especially complex and sensitive geopolitical moment, in their handling of the miners’ deaths. While he insisted that Monday’s shootings came down to the actions of an individual, Ali warned Khartoum and Cairo against allowing their opponents further opportunities to exploit the miners’ deaths. “The matter should be closed by clarifying the facts, identifying who is responsible and holding them accountable,” he said. “The Sudanese government must also take responsibility for securing the borders and regulating miners’ activity in accordance with the law.” Two days after the strike, the Transitional Sovereignty Council issued its first comment on the incident, announcing the formation of a fact-finding committee to investigate the deaths of the Sudanese miners. While the statement said Egyptian and Sudanese leaders had remained in contact since the attack to establish the facts, Egypt’s military announced later that evening that it had launched the third phase of its campaign against illegal gold mining in the Eastern Desert, citing the protection of national resources and the imposition of Egypt’s “full sovereignty” over its territories, without acknowledgement of the incident. According to a senior Sudanese diplomat, TSC Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan is paying close attention to the matter amid mounting public pressure to uncover the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible. That level of attention reflects heightened public concern in Sudan and the need to manage the strikes’ repercussions through state institutions and official channels, while safeguarding Sudanese citizens’ rights and ensuring the incident is treated seriously, the source said. The diplomatic steps are intended to convey Khartoum’s position to Cairo clearly and facilitate cooperation between the relevant authorities to complete the investigation and address questions raised by the incident, the diplomat added. Sudan has put forward a proposal for a joint security matrix to govern how incidents and activities in border areas are handled, define the responsibilities of relevant agencies and establish coordination mechanisms, according to the diplomat. The proposal also calls for the activation of surveillance and field monitoring procedures in areas prone to such incidents, he added. The matrix could include direct communication channels between relevant agencies in both countries, clear procedures for reporting and verifying incidents and mechanisms for sharing information on movements and activities requiring security intervention. It could also prompt a review of how authorities respond when incidents affect citizens or people working in border areas, the diplomat said. The proposal’s significance lies in the shift from responding to each incident separately toward an institutional mechanism for managing border risks and preventing the recurrence of similar incidents, the source added. Activating surveillance mechanisms would require practical coordination between the relevant Sudanese and Egyptian agencies, potentially through a new joint committee similar to the long established bodies overseeing other aspects of Sudanese-Egyptian affairs. This would necessitates clearly defined administrative and security responsibilities and a mechanism for exchanging information and verifying reports, the source said. All adopted measures would need to respect the sovereignty of both countries and the rules governing activities in border areas, the source added. An Egyptian official briefed on Egyptian-Sudanese relations confirmed that Cairo is considering establishing a joint security presence on the border alongside the Sudanese military to ensure border security. Egypt has pointed to the plan in discussions with African Union officials, during which Saturday’s strikes were criticized. An informed diplomat said Egypt had informed AU officials of its ongoing coordination with Sudan on measures and criteria for joint border management. The post Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Trade Minister urges employers to leverage industrial opportunities to create jobs
items.description: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has urged employers to take advantage of the government’s industrial policies and investment opportunities to expand businesses, boost productivity and create jobs. She said economic stabilisation measures, alongside targeted industrial policies and investments in energy, digital trade systems and export development, were creating an enabling environment for businesses to grow and compete in domestic and international markets. Madam Ofosu-Adjare made the call when she addressed the 66th Annual General Meeting of the Ghana Employers’ Association (GEA) in Accra on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. She outlined the government’s strategies to move Ghana from economic stabilisation towards production-led growth, emphasising the role of the private sector in driving investment, industrial expansion and employment creation. The Minister congratulated the leadership and members of the Association on the milestone, describing the GEA as a critical partner in national development and an important voice in shaping policies that affect businesses and employment. “Through every political turn and every economic cycle, your association has remained a steady backbone, never ceasing to advocate for employers, the people who create the bulk of the jobs. We salute you for this,” she said. The meeting was held under the theme, “Macroeconomic Stability, Policy Predictability and Employment Creation in Ghana.” Meanwhile, the President-elect of the Association, Nana Dr Emmanuel Adu-Sarkodee, in a speech read on his behalf, commended stakeholders for renewing their mandate and pledged a stronger commitment to serving the employer community. He also proposed the institutionalisation of a Policy Predictability Compact (PPC) between the government and the private sector to promote a more predictable policy environment for businesses.

items.title: Burkina/Passeport biométrique: la fin des longues distances pour les citoyens des régions
items.description: Le Camarade ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou SANA, a procédé au lancement officiel de l'extension du service d'enrôlement des passeports à l'ensemble des régions du Burkina Faso, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026 à Ziniaré, dans la région d'Oubri. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence de la Gouverneure de la région d'Oubri, la Camarade Sy Assétou BARRY/TRAORÉ, ainsi que des corps constitués. Pour le ministre SANA, cette initiative traduit une exigence fondamentale de l'action publique : faire du service public un droit accessible à tous, et non une contrainte imposée par la distance. Il a, à cet effet, exhorté l'ensemble des acteurs concernés à faire de cette réforme une réussite, en garantissant un accueil de qualité et des procédures d'enrôlement et de délivrance des passeports plus accessibles, diligentes, transparentes et sécurisées. « Au-delà de l'enrôlement des passeports, cette initiative porte une ambition claire : rapprocher durablement l'administration des citoyens et rendre le service public plus accessible partout au Burkina Faso », a-t-il souligné, en insistant sur la nécessité d'assurer le bon fonctionnement du dispositif dans toutes les régions.» La Gouverneure de la région d'Oubri, la Camarade Sy Assétou BARRY/TRAORÉ, a salué le choix de sa région pour accueillir le lancement de cette réforme. Elle a, par ailleurs, invité l'ensemble des corps constitués à accompagner son déploiement afin d'en garantir le succès. Cette extension marque ainsi une étape importante dans le rapprochement de l’administration des populations et la facilitation des démarches liées à l’obtention du passeport biométrique sur l'ensemble du territoire national. items.title: Reps order halt to disputed land development in Imo
items.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Public Petitions has ordered a halt to further development on a disputed parcel of land in Umundoche community, Ngor Okpala Local Government Area of Imo State, pending the resolution of a petition alleging illegal land acquisition and intimidation of residents. The committee also directed that armed men allegedly operating in the community be disarmed following claims that villagers had been threatened with firearms amid the dispute. The directives were issued on Wednesday during a hearing on Petition No. 901 of 2026, filed by J.U. Okoye Chambers against Prince Charles Amadi, also known as Chavon; Chikadibia Anyanwu; and Chidubem Nwosu. The petition alleges the illegal acquisition of more than 2,500 hectares of land, shooting and attempted murder of villagers, the invasion of the community by armed men, desecration of a corpse, abuse of police powers and breach of a memorandum of understanding. The petition also names HRH Eze Lambert Unuoha, traditional ruler of Nma 1 of Obioma Autonomous Community in Ngor Okpala, as a respondent. Addressing the parties, the committee chairman, who was represented by his deputy, Rep. Matthew Nwogu, directed that no further activity should take place on the disputed land until the matter was resolved through the committee or other appropriate means. “There are orders that no more actions on this land until this matter is resolved,” the chairman said. “Either through this place, or through which other means you want to resolve it. That’s the first order. No more putting up caterpillars or bulldozers in that land.” He said the committee had contacted the Department of State Services (DSS) and the police, which, according to him, denied supplying firearms to the men allegedly operating in the community. “All the boys that are armed in that village should be disarmed. Because we have made contact with the DSS. They said they didn’t give them the gun. The police said they didn’t,” he said. The chairman said the directives were intended to prevent further escalation while the committee examined the allegations. The hearing featured disagreements among lawyers representing the parties over the status of a pending court case and whether the committee should continue considering the petition. Counsel to Charles Farms Limited, identified during the proceedings as one of the parties involved in the dispute, told the committee that his clients had legally acquired the land and paid the relevant parties. He rejected the allegations in the petition and disclosed that his clients had instituted legal proceedings against the petitioners. According to him, he wrote to the committee on September 28, 2026, explaining his clients’ position and providing details of the court proceedings. He, however, acknowledged that he had not brought the supporting court documents to the hearing. The committee chairman said a letter and oral explanations were insufficient, demanding certified documentary evidence to establish the status of the case. The lawyer subsequently undertook to organise the documents he had received, certify the necessary papers and submit them to the committee. A committee member, intervening in the exchange, cautioned against allowing the existence of a court case to automatically terminate the legislative investigation. He said the committee had a constitutional responsibility to consider petitions submitted to it, adding that the scope of the court proceedings would have to be examined before determining whether they covered all the issues raised in the petition. “That a matter is in court does not immediately stop us from doing our duty. This is a constitutional committee. One of the very few committees written into the Nigerian constitution,” the lawmaker said. He urged the parties to respect the committee’s procedures and allow the petitioners an opportunity to present their grievances. “Tomorrow he might be the one petitioning this National Assembly over an issue. So let us respect processes, respect our constitution. And then respect the will of the people who have come here to seek justice,” he added. The lawmaker also urged the committee to give the respondents time to file formal responses, noting that the proceedings would benefit from documentary evidence from both sides. Petitioners allege intimidation of villagers Counsel to the petitioners, Dr Julius Onyemi, told the committee that efforts had been made to resolve the dispute before the matter was brought before the House. He said the first petition was submitted on July 17, 2026, followed by another on August 14 and a subsequent petition later that month. Onyemi alleged that he had made several attempts to contact the respondents to resolve the dispute with the community but was unsuccessful. He further alleged that the court action was initiated after the petitions had been submitted to the House and suggested that it was intended to frustrate the committee’s proceedings. The lawyer also accused the respondents of using security personnel and armed men to intimidate residents and prevent them from accessing their community. He urged the committee to ensure that the alleged intimidation stopped while the petition was being considered. Onyemi questioned the circumstances surrounding the land acquisition and called on the parties to demonstrate compliance with customary land acquisition procedures. He also raised concerns about the environmental implications of the proposed development, asking whether an environmental impact assessment had been conducted and made available to the community. The lawyer argued that residents had a right to be consulted over activities that could affect their land and environment. The respondents’ representatives disputed the allegations, maintaining that the land had been legally acquired. The claims remain subject to the committee’s investigation. Committee demands video evidence During the hearing, one of the respondents’ representatives challenged claims that armed men had visited the community and threatened residents. He said he had been in the area since Monday and disputed claims that he was present at the location where the alleged incident occurred. He offered to provide his flight itinerary and hotel booking details to support his account. The chairman subsequently asked the parties to provide any available video or photographic evidence to establish what happened. He said the committee was interested in examining the available evidence rather than relying solely on conflicting oral accounts. The chairman reiterated that further development on the disputed land must stop and that armed men allegedly involved in intimidating residents must be disarmed. The committee adjourned the matter until November 2026 to allow the respondents to study the petition, prepare their formal responses and submit the necessary documentary evidence. The hearing formed part of the committee’s consideration of the petition seeking intervention over the disputed land in Umundoche community, Imo State. The allegations have not been established as findings of fact. The respondents maintain that the land was legally acquired, while the committee is yet to conclude its investigation. items.title: Kankan : le double message de Djénabou Touré aux autorités locales et aux citoyens
items.description: « Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ne peut pas rester à Conakry et voir tout ce qui se passe en Guinée ou dans les villages. Tout ce qui se gâte, on dit son nom, pourtant nous sommes censés faire le travail. Nous avons notre responsabilité là-dedans » À Kankan, la ministre de l’Administration du Territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djénabou Touré, appelle à un respect mutuel entre les autorités et les citoyens. Lors d’une rencontre tenue ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026 à la Maison des jeunes de Kankan, elle a exhorté les populations à respecter les autorités établies, tout en rappelant aux responsables locaux leur obligation de répondre aux préoccupations des citoyens. Elle a également insisté sur le rôle des chefs de quartier dans la lutte contre le banditisme et l’amélioration des conditions de vie des habitants. Évoquant les critiques relatives au manque de respect envers les chefs traditionnels et les autorités en Haute-Guinée, la ministre a invité les citoyens à abandonner les comportements qu’elle juge contraires aux valeurs de respect de l’autorité. « On dit que quand on vient chez nous en Haute-Guinée, c’est ici qu’il y a le non-respect des chefs. Il faut qu’on abandonne cela, ce n’est pas bon. Respectons nos chefs… », a-t-elle déclaré, rappelant l’importance du respect des lois et des institutions pour le bon fonctionnement de l’administration. Pour Djénabou Touré, les sous-préfets, les préfets, les gouverneurs et les maires occupent des fonctions qui leur confèrent des responsabilités précises dans la gestion des affaires publiques. Le respect dû à ces autorités doit, selon elle, contribuer au fonctionnement harmonieux de l’État. Mais la ministre a également tenu à rappeler que l’autorité ne saurait se résumer à un statut ou à une fonction. Les responsables locaux doivent, en retour, faire preuve d’écoute et se préoccuper des difficultés quotidiennes des populations. L’accès à l’eau potable, aux soins de santé, à l’éducation, à la sécurité ainsi que la bonne gestion des espaces publics figurent parmi les préoccupations qu’elle a mises en avant. Elle a ainsi appelé chaque responsable à s’investir davantage dans la recherche de solutions concrètes aux problèmes des citoyens. Dans cette dynamique, Djénabou Touré a souligné que le développement du pays ne saurait reposer uniquement sur le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya. Elle a invité les responsables à assumer pleinement leur part de responsabilité dans la gestion des affaires publiques. « Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ne peut pas rester à Conakry et voir tout ce qui se passe en Guinée ou dans les villages. Tout ce qui se gâte, on dit son nom, pourtant nous sommes censés faire le travail. Nous avons notre responsabilité là-dedans », a-t-elle souligné. À travers cette déclaration, la ministre a appelé les responsables administratifs et locaux à prendre leurs responsabilités et à s’impliquer davantage dans la résolution des problèmes auxquels les populations sont confrontées. La lutte contre le banditisme a également occupé une place importante dans son intervention. Djénabou Touré a notamment exhorté les chefs de quartier à renforcer leur collaboration avec les services de sécurité afin de mieux prévenir les actes criminels. Elle leur a demandé de signaler aux autorités compétentes les zones sensibles de leurs quartiers et de contribuer activement à la sécurisation de leurs communautés. Cette démarche vise à renforcer le rôle des responsables de proximité dans la prévention de l’insécurité et la protection des citoyens. Au terme de cette rencontre, la ministre a mis en avant une double exigence : le respect des autorités légalement établies et le devoir de celles-ci de servir les populations avec responsabilité. Pour Djénabou Touré, l’amélioration des conditions de vie et le développement de la Guinée nécessitent l’engagement de tous les acteurs, des responsables administratifs aux citoyens. Chacun est ainsi appelé à jouer pleinement son rôle, dans le respect des lois et des responsabilités qui lui incombent.
