items.title: 2027: Accreditation, collation won’t be fully automated – INEC
items.description: …Says Nigerians, not AI, will determine election outcomes By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has assured Nigerians that voter accreditation and result collation will not be fully automated in the 2027 general elections, insisting that citizens, not Artificial Intelligence AI, will determine the outcome. Chairman of the Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN said on Wednesday that “Algorithms will not, and must never, decide the 2027 vote.” INEC in its Wednesday Bulletin said Amupitan spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026, held in collaboration with Yiaga Africa. Amupitan said, as a foundational policy, no critical electoral decision, result collation, voter accreditation or candidate qualification would ever be fully automated or delegated to an autonomous system. “Human accountability, statutory oversight and judicial review will remain paramount at every stage of the electoral chain,” he said. Responding to the forum’s opening question, “Will Algorithms Decide the 2027 Vote?”, he said the answer was an unequivocal no. According to him, the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people. The chairman said the forum was taking place 92 days before the general elections, in a digital landscape that had shifted significantly since 2023. He warned that the Commission was no longer dealing only with the “analogue” challenges of logistics but with a world in which AI can influence what a voter sees, how the voter thinks and how the voter trusts. “The greatest threat we face is not the hacking of a ballot box, but the hacking of the voter’s mind,” Amupitan stated. He said generative AI had reduced to near zero the cost of producing convincing deepfakes, including videos of candidates saying things they never said and of INEC officials giving false instructions. “If a voter cannot distinguish between truth and a synthetic lie, the foundation of informed consent crumbles,” he said. The INEC chairman warned that a well-timed deepfake video or cloned audio recording of a candidate, an election official or a security chief could announce a false candidate withdrawal, a postponement of the election or inflammatory ethnoreligious statements, and spread virally within minutes. He added that malicious actors could also impersonate the INEC Chairman, Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs and other officials to issue fake guidelines, declare unauthorised results or instruct voters to stay home. On the Commission’s response, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had created an AI Unit within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Directorate, equipped with real-time digital monitoring tools, deepfake detection software and data analytics expertise. He said any AI tool or automated system deployed by the Commission for logistics, database management or operational support must undergo rigorous audits to guarantee explainability, fairness and security before deployment. The Commission, he added, was working on a Digital Strategy to audit the information environment and partnering with technology platforms for the rapid debunking and labelling of AI-generated content touching on electoral processes. Amupitan called on technology companies, including Meta, X, Google, TikTok and Telegram, to rapidly restrict unlabelled synthetic media impersonating election officials, candidates or security personnel. He also asked them to enforce disclaimers on political advertisements and restrict micro-targeting based on ethnicity, religion or local origin. He urged political parties and candidates to sign an Ethical AI Code of Conduct, committing to refrain from deploying deepfakes, synthetic impersonation, dark ads or automated botnets. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission does not view AI only through the prism of risk. He described it as a powerful force multiplier for administrative precision, predictive planning and institutional integrity. He said while human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring results, AI could run parallel statistical audits on polling unit result sheets uploaded through the eEC8A, flagging mathematical inconsistencies, atypical entry patterns and image quality defects for administrative review. On logistics, he said AI-driven geospatial analytics could help INEC deploy ad-hoc staff, vehicles, boats and sensitive materials to 176,846 polling units before 7:30 a.m. on election day. Amupitan said the 2027 General Election would be the largest democratic exercise on the African continent, involving over 103 million registered voters across 774 Local Government Areas LGAs. He said 10 of the 14 major operational milestones under the Electoral Act 2026 had been successfully executed. The two-day forum was attended by the Chairperson of the Economic Community of West African States Network of Electoral Commissions ECONEC and Chairman of the Senegal Electoral Commission, Mr Abdoulaye Sylla, along with National Commissioners, RECs, political party leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies, technology firms and the media. Amupitan said algorithms had no moral compass, no civic duty and no constitutional oath. “They do not have a conscience, they do not have a country, and they do not have a vote. INEC’s job is to ensure that the voice of the people is heard clearly, above the noise of the machines. “On election day in 2027, it will be the thumbprint of the Nigerian citizen, guided by their own will and their own hopes, that decides our future,” Amupitan said. The post 2027: Accreditation, collation won’t be fully automated – INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cancer : le gouvernement actualise son plan national avant le 31 décembre
items.description: Derrière chaque diagnostic de cancer, il y a une bataille qui ne se limite pas au traitement médical. Il faut pouvoir accéder à un spécialiste, réaliser les examens nécessaires, trouver les médicaments prescrits et financer un parcours de soins parfois long. Pour de nombreuses familles, ces contraintes peuvent s’ajouter à l’épreuve de la maladie. C’est dans ce contexte que le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed LO a annoncé, lors du Conseil des ministres du 13 octobre, l’actualisation du Plan national de lutte contre le cancer 2025-2029, au plus tard le 31 décembre 2026. Le Gouvernement prévoit également de sécuriser la disponibilité des médicaments anticancéreux et de faciliter l’enrôlement des malades démunis dans les dispositifs de prise en charge de l’Agence de la Couverture sanitaire universelle. 14 358 cas en 2024 : l’ampleur du défi Les chiffres disponibles donnent la mesure du défi. Selon les estimations de GLOBOCAN 2024, publiées par le Centre international de recherche sur le cancer, une agence de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé, le Sénégal a enregistré environ 14 358 nouveaux cas de cancer et 9 659 décès cette année-là. Les femmes représentaient 8 670 des nouveaux cas estimés. Les cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein étaient les plus fréquents chez elles, avec respectivement 2 280 et 2 220 cas estimés. Ces données sont des estimations modélisées et non un décompte exhaustif de chaque diagnostic. Elles montrent néanmoins le poids de la maladie et l’importance d’une stratégie qui ne se limite pas aux soins hospitaliers. Pour les cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein, l’information, le dépistage et l’orientation rapide vers des services adaptés sont des maillons essentiels. Plus une maladie est repérée tôt, plus les équipes médicales disposent de possibilités pour organiser la prise en charge. L’actualisation du plan national doit donc permettre de préciser les priorités, les responsabilités et les moyens. Elle gagnerait à s’appuyer sur des objectifs mesurables : améliorer l’accès au dépistage, réduire les délais avant le diagnostic, renforcer la disponibilité des traitements et suivre les patients tout au long de leur parcours. La coordination entre les structures sanitaires, les professionnels, les associations et les collectivités est tout aussi importante pour atteindre les personnes qui consultent tardivement ou vivent loin des services spécialisés. Médicaments, couverture sanitaire : de l’annonce à l’accès La question des médicaments est tout aussi déterminante. Une prescription ne suffit pas si le produit n’est pas disponible ou reste financièrement inaccessible. Le communiqué ne précise ni la liste des médicaments concernés ni les moyens prévus pour en sécuriser l’approvisionnement. Ces éléments devront être clarifiés pour apprécier la portée concrète de la mesure annoncée. Le soutien aux patients les plus démunis constitue un autre enjeu. L’enrôlement dans les dispositifs de couverture sanitaire peut alléger une partie des dépenses, mais son efficacité dépendra des critères d’éligibilité, de la simplicité des démarches et de la couverture réelle des prestations. Il faudra notamment préciser les examens, les traitements et les frais pris en charge, ainsi que les modalités d’accès aux structures spécialisées. La date du 31 décembre 2026 fixe une échéance pour l’actualisation du plan. Le défi commencera ensuite : transformer les orientations en services accessibles, avec des ressources identifiées et un suivi public des résultats. Pour les malades, l’efficacité de la politique se mesurera moins au nombre de documents adoptés qu’à la possibilité d’être diagnostiqué à temps, de recevoir le traitement prescrit et de poursuivre les soins sans basculer dans la précarité. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: ADC accuses APC of coercing opposition governors into campaign council
items.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of coercing opposition governors into its presidential campaign council, alleging that the ruling party is undermining Nigeria’s multiparty democracy ahead of the 2027 general election. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council’s Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, made the allegation in a statement reacting to the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Wednesday. Ologbondiyan accused the ruling party of using state power to pressure opposition governors into its fold or include them in its campaign structure despite their continued membership of other political parties. “What we are witnessing is not politics but political abduction. You cannot claim to be a democrat while using state power to force opposition governors into your party and then drafting them into your campaign council. This is political banditry,” he said. The ADC spokesman also alleged that the APC was pursuing a political agenda aimed at concentrating power in the hands of one individual, claiming that national institutions, security agencies and the judiciary were being deployed to weaken opposition forces. He urged Nigerians to resist what he described as an attempt to establish an immoral political order driven by the desire to retain power at the expense of citizens’ welfare. Ologbondiyan further accused the ruling party of neglecting the economic hardship, hunger and insecurity confronting Nigerians while focusing on its political interests. “These particular sets of leaders don’t care about the current conditions of the people but how best to remain in power at a time when average Nigerians find it difficult to eat and be secure,” he said. He also alleged that the country’s democratic space was shrinking, citing what he described as the suppression of dissenting voices, harassment of opposition figures and the weakening of democratic institutions for partisan purposes. “Never in our democratic journey have we witnessed this level of intolerance and desperation. The APC government has weaponised poverty, hunger and insecurity to subjugate Nigerians and cripple the opposition,” Ologbondiyan said. He added that the situation was inconsistent with the democratic ideals for which late politician Moshood Abiola and other pro-democracy figures fought. The ADC spokesman also promoted the party’s presidential ticket of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, describing them as having the experience and democratic credentials to address the country’s challenges. “Atiku Abubakar is a democrat to the core. He has the national spread, the capacity and the will to reunite Nigeria and restore our battered democracy,” he said. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council called on Nigerians, media organisations, civil society groups and the international community to oppose what it described as the APC’s anti-democratic agenda and support efforts to protect multiparty democracy. items.title: Asantehene plants trees to commence Jimi Watercourse Rehabilitation destroyed by galamsey
items.description: The Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, has planted trees at the Jimi River near Obuasi to launch a major effort to reclaim lands and restore the river destroyed by illegal mining. He visited Lot 1 of the Jimi Land Reclamation and River Watercourse Rehabilitation Project, a 153-hectare pilot under the Green Ashanti Initiative, to inspect ongoing works and symbolically plant trees to mark the restoration. The site, which holds a major water source for the Adansi enclave, has been heavily degraded by galamsey, with vegetation stripped, soils contaminated and open pits left behind. The pollution threatens the Jimi River and the Jimi Dam downstream, which treats water for over 200,000 people in Obuasi and the Adansi area. At Tasliman, illegal miners have diverted the course of the river with heaps of sand, causing heavy siltation and rising turbidity. Aside from the rising turbidity levels, which has increased the cost of water treatment, the dam’s volume is decreasing, hence resulting in rationing of water to the communities. Director of Engineering at AngloGold Ashanti, Ing. Eric Broni, says the impact is already hitting water supply. “There is a possibility that this year, water abstraction will decrease. When the water level drops, abstraction decreases, but our cost increases. Last year we spent about $584,000 to treat water despite treating less. It is becoming a worry because we have to ration water to other communities,” he said. The Jimi project, led by the Ashanti Green Initiative under the leadership of Oheneba Nana Kwaku Duah, with Manhyia Palace providing vision and patronage, is piloting a six-step restoration model: backfilling pits, re-grading spoil heaps and terracing slopes, containing heavy metal contamination, installing drainage and erosion controls, restoring topsoil, and replanting with kenaf. Kenaf, a fast-growing fibre crop for sacks, ropes and eco-composites and other uses, has been chosen over food crops due to residual contamination risk and to provide alternative livelihoods for local farmers. The Jimi River and its buffer zones will also be cleaned and replanted under EPA guidance. The Asantehene was joined by partners, including AngloGold Ashanti, which is providing technical and operational support. The Managing Director, Samuel Boakye Pobee, said, “We are proud to be partners in the fight against land degradation and elated by the government’s support. The Jimi remains important to Obuasi. It provides water to many people outside the mine, more than those in the mine.” Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, disclosed that about 8,000 hectares of 188 forest reserves have been impacted by galamsey, with only 150 hectares reclaimed so far. “Government can only succeed with partnership. 80% of water comes from forest reserves, and this goes to the core of human survival. Government is committed to this partnership. The Asantehene’s commitment is a model for all chiefs,” he said. Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, described the project as a national crusade. “What you are doing is the launching of a national crusade for traditional leaders to partner with civil society, mining companies and government to lead the way to restore degraded lands,” he said. Organisers say the Green Ashanti tree planting at Jimi is more than symbolic. It marks the start of a replicable model to restore Ghana’s degraded lands, protect clean water, and restore livelihoods. The Asantehene was briefed at AngloGold Ashanti in Obuasi before moving to Lot 1 for the tree planting and inspection of the reclamation site and later, the Jimi Dam.

items.title: Justice pénale : le Parlement adopte une réforme clé du travail d’intérêt général
items.description: Réunis en séance plénière le mercredi 14 octobre 2026, sous la présidence du chef du Parlement, le camarade Dr Ousmane BOUGOUMA, les 71 députés votants ont adopté à l’unanimité le projet de loi révisé portant administration du travail d’intérêt général (TIG) au Burkina Faso. Bien qu’ayant enregistré des résultats encourageants, la loi n°035-2024/ALT du 8 novembre 2024 portant administration du travail d’intérêt général présentait plusieurs insuffisances qui ont rendu nécessaire sa révision. Le nouveau texte vise à renforcer la réinsertion sociale des personnes condamnées et à contribuer au désengorgement des établissements pénitentiaires. Parmi les principales innovations figurent le prononcé d’office du TIG pour certaines infractions mineures, l’élargissement des activités éligibles aux prestations intellectuelles et l’instauration d’un régime permanent de commutation des peines d’emprisonnement en travail d’intérêt général. À travers cette adoption, l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP) contribue à l’évolution du dispositif pénal en faveur d’une justice qui privilégie la responsabilisation des personnes condamnées, leur réinsertion sociale et l’utilité collective. items.title: 15 arrested, 6 trucks impounded over sandwinning activities on Kumasi-Accra Expressway
items.description: The National Security in the Ashanti region has arrested fifteen individuals for their alleged involvement in sandwinning activities on the Kumasi–Accra Expressway project. The suspects, all males, were apprehended in the Sewua–Donyina–Appiadu enclave during a swoop by some officers of the National Security on Wednesday, October 14. Six trucks, including a wheel loader, were also impounded during the raid in the enclave. An Assistant Liaison Officer, Ivan Bilson Yeboah, says the suspects have been transported to the national office in Accra for custody and further investigations. “They are on their way to Accra for our officers at the headquarters to carry out further investigations,” he said. A viral video indicated the individuals have been excavating and removing white sand from the Accra-Kumasi Expressway for commercial purposes. This raised concerns about the potential destruction of the right of way, which is crucial to the planned road infrastructure. Mr. Yeboah described the illegal activity as unacceptable, advising the public to desist from such practices, which impede national development. “We have seen a considerable damage being done to the road. It’s bad that resources of the state will be channeled to such a beautiful national activity, but people who want to loot and do whatever they did. This is unacceptable. Mr. Bilson Yeboah further noted that the regional security council is expected to meet to deliberate on means to heighten patrols along the portion of the expressway in the region. “REGSEC will be meeting on Thursday to look at how to sustain surveillance on the stretch to nip some of these activities in the bud,” he noted. However, some suspects remain at large as the security force intensifies the manhunt for their whereabouts. Bosomtwe District Chief Executive, Ing. Abdullah Hamidu, disclosed exclusively to JoyNews that preliminary investigations by the Assembly suggested the sand winners claimed to have obtained authorization from the Ejisu Municipality Assembly to undertake the excavation. They, however, failed to produce a copy of the said permit. “When they were directed to my office, they told me they had obtained a permit from Ejisu, but they could not provide a copy. I ordered them to stop the operation and referred the matter to the police for further investigations,” he said.

items.title: Senate urges FERMA to repair failed Anambra-Rivers highway
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Senate has urged the Federal Road Maintenance Agency (FERMA) to undertake emergency repairs on failed sections of the Onitsha–Ogbaru–Ndoni–Rivers Federal Highway pending its comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction. The Senate said the immediate intervention would reduce the hardship faced by motorists and communities along the route. Following a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North, the Senate also proposed that the Federal Government mandate the South East Development Commission (SEDC) or the Federal Ministry of Works to carry out the remedial work. The Senate recommended that the comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction be executed through a special intervention programme or another appropriate funding arrangement, given the road’s strategic importance as a major link between the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones. It mandated the Senate Committee on Works to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of the highway, engage relevant stakeholders and report back within four weeks with appropriate recommendations. It also urged the Senate committees on Works and Appropriations to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the road’s comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction. The Senate noted that the highway was partially constructed in the late 1980s but had suffered decades of neglect without any major rehabilitation. It said the prolonged abandonment, ageing infrastructure, increasing traffic volume and lack of routine maintenance had left the road in a deplorable condition, characterised by extensive pavement failures, deep potholes and severe erosion. According to the Senate, the condition of the highway posed a serious threat to the lives and property of commuters and other road users. It further observed that the deterioration had significantly increased travel time, with a journey of approximately 70 kilometres from Onitsha through Ogbaru to Ndoni, which would ordinarily take about one hour, now taking nearly two hours. The Senate said the situation had resulted in higher transportation costs, loss of productive man-hours and disruption of commercial activities. It added that the failed sections frequently caused vehicles to break down and remain stranded for extended periods, exposing commuters to road accidents and heightened security risks. The Senate also noted that the highway served as a vital economic corridor, supporting significant oil and gas exploration and production activities in the Ogbaru oil belt and contributing to Nigeria’s economy. It expressed concern that continued neglect of the federal highway had affected interstate commerce, agricultural value chains, regional integration and investment, undermining efforts to promote economic development, national connectivity and safe transportation. The Senate warned that without urgent intervention, further deterioration would endanger lives and property, impede economic activities, increase transportation costs and affect oil exploration and production along the Ogbaru corridor. It added that the situation would worsen the hardship faced by residents of Anambra and Rivers states and negatively affect businesses that depend on the transport corridor. The post Senate urges FERMA to repair failed Anambra-Rivers highway appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La réouverture de la route 463 aux colons menace d’isoler Ramallah
items.description: L'armee israelienne s'apprete a rouvrir aux colons la route 463, un axe de dix kilometres traversant le nord de Ramallah et d'el-Bireh. Cette mesure, selon plusieurs sources, menacerait d'isoler huit villages palestiniens et deux grands quartiers residentiels, tout en separant le nord et le sud du gouvernorat. Une route au cœur de la fragmentation Construite au milieu des annees 1990 pour relier les colonies de Beit El et de Dolev, la route 463 avait ete fermee apres le declenchement de la seconde Intifada. Sa reouverture s'inscrit dans un budget d'infrastructures de 1,075 milliard de shekels (environ 355 millions de dollars) destine aux colonies, illegales au regard du droit international. Le gouvernement israelien souhaite accelerer le processus avant les elections du 27 octobre . La Commission de resistance a la colonisation et au mur, affiliee a l'OLP, denonce une « politique systematique visant a demanteler la contiguïte geographique et demographique palestinienne ». Des dizaines de milliers d'habitants seraient contraints d'emprunter une route alternative deja saturee pres du camp de Jalazone. Les villages de Surda, at-Tira, Ein Qiniya, Ras Karkar, Deir Ibzi ou Ein Arik seraient particulierement touches. Jamal Juma, coordinateur de la Campagne populaire de resistance au mur et aux colonies, estime que la reouverture « encerclerait completement la partie ouest de Ramallah ». Sur X, l'Association France Palestine Solidarite avait deja alerte le 1er octobre en soulignant que « l'armee et les colons israeliens collaborent pour rouvrir la route 463 reservee aux colons et rompre la continuite territoriale ». L'armée et les colons israéliens collaborent pour rouvrir la route 463 réservée aux colons et rompre la continuité territoriale. Selon Jamal Jumaa de @stopthewall, elle divisera Ramallah en coupant les universités dont Birzeit du reste de la ville. https://t.co/Icp4rZ426c — Association France Palestine Solidarité (@AFPSOfficiel) October 1, 2026 Munif Treish, maire d'El-Bireh, rappelle que 95 % du trace se situe en zone B, placee sous administration civile palestinienne selon les accords d'Oslo II. Il y voit une « violation flagrante » des engagements pris avec l'OLP et une « menace existentielle » pour 250 000 Palestiniens. La municipalite promet de mobiliser tous les moyens legaux pour s'y opposer tandis que la mobilisation internationale, notamment au sein de l'UE, ne semble pour l'heure pas produire d'effets .
